```
1	# Contact Manager
2	
3	**ContactManager** is a native, modern macOS desktop application demonstrating best practices in desktop architecture, persistence, and unit testing.
4	
5	The project is **100% self-contained and standalone**, featuring zero third-party dependencies. It has been fully modernized to target macOS 13.0+ and compiles under modern Xcode toolchains with zero warnings.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Key Modernization Features
10	
11	1. **Modern Persistence Stack**:
12	   - Replaced legacy manual Core Data lifecycle management with Apple's standard **`NSPersistentContainer`** framework.
13	   - Core Data stores are fully loaded synchronously on initialization for deterministic runtime behavior.
14	   - Built-in automatic migration support and clean directory setup inside standard Application Support paths.
15	
16	2. **Objective-C Modernization**:
17	   - **Full Nullability Coverage**: Entire codebase annotated with `NS_ASSUME_NONNULL` and proper pointer specifiers (`nonnull`, `nullable`) for complete type safety and seamless Swift interoperability.
18	   - **Type-Safe Generics**: Standardized all collections (e.g. `NSArray<Contact *> *` and `NSFetchRequest<__kindof NSManagedObject *> *`) to enable compile-time type checking.
19	   - **Memory Safety**: Converted delegates and interface outlets to modern `weak` pointers to eliminate risk of retain cycles.
20	   - **Unavailable Initializers**: Standardized designated initializers and marked legacy default `init`/`new` initializers as `NS_UNAVAILABLE` to guarantee correct instance construction.
21	
22	3. **Zero-Dependency Testing**:
23	   - Swapped out the legacy third-party `OCMock` framework in favor of lightweight native testing constructs.
24	   - Integration tests are backed by a real, blazing-fast, in-memory Core Data stack (`NSInMemoryStoreType`), executing type-safe code without polluting local developer filesystems.
25	   - Subclassed view controllers directly inside the test target to spy on KVO bindings.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Tech Stack & Architecture
30	
31	- **Platform**: macOS 13.0+ (AppKit)
32	- **Language**: Objective-C (Automatic Reference Counting, LLVM Modules enabled)
33	- **Database**: Core Data (`NSPersistentContainer`)
34	- **UI Binding**: Cocoa Bindings & Key-Value Observing (KVO)
35	- **Unit Testing**: XCTest
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Getting Started
40	
41	### Prerequisites
42	
43	No dependency managers (such as Carthage, CocoaPods, or Swift Package Manager) are required.
44	
45	To prepare the local homebrew build environment (if any tools are missing):
46	```shell
47	./scripts/bootstrap.sh
48	```
49	
50	### Building & Running
51	
52	Open `ContactManager.xcodeproj` in Xcode and select the **ContactManager** scheme. Press `Cmd + R` to build and run.
53	
54	### Running the Test Suite
55	
56	To run all 31 unit tests directly from the command line:
57	```shell
58	xcodebuild -project ContactManager.xcodeproj -scheme ContactManager -configuration Debug test
59	```
```

37	{

39	    
40	    self = [super init];
41		if (self) {
42			_initialType = type;
43	        _modelName = theModelName;
44	        if (![_initialType isEqualToString:NSInMemoryStoreType]) {
45	            NSParameterAssert(theApplicationSupportName != nil);

57	- (NSString *)applicationSupportFolder 
58	{
59	    NSArray *paths = NSSearchPathForDirectoriesInDomains(NSApplicationSupportDirectory, NSUserDomainMask, YES);
60	    NSString *basePath = ([paths count] > 0) ? paths[0] : NSTemporaryDirectory();
61		return [basePath stringByAppendingPathComponent:_appSupportName];
62	}
63	
64	- (NSManagedObjectModel *)managedObjectModel 
65	{
66	    if (_managedObjectModel != nil) {
67	        return _managedObjectModel;
68	    }
69		
70		NSURL *modelUrl = [[NSBundle mainBundle] URLForResource:[_modelName stringByDeletingPathExtension] withExtension:[_modelName pathExtension]];
71	    _managedObjectModel = [[NSManagedObjectModel alloc] initWithContentsOfURL:modelUrl];
72	    return _managedObjectModel;
73	}

75	- (NSPersistentContainer *)persistentContainer
76	{
77	    if (_persistentContainer != nil) {
78	        return _persistentContainer;
79	    }
80	    
81	    NSString *containerName = [_modelName stringByDeletingPathExtension];
82	    _persistentContainer = [[NSPersistentContainer alloc] initWithName:containerName managedObjectModel:[self managedObjectModel]];
83	    
84	    NSPersistentStoreDescription *storeDescription;
85	    if ([_initialType isEqualToString:NSInMemoryStoreType]) {
86	        storeDescription = [NSPersistentStoreDescription persistentStoreDescriptionWithURL:[NSURL fileURLWithPath:@"/dev/null"]];
87	    } else {
88	        NSFileManager *fileManager = [NSFileManager defaultManager];
89	        NSString *applicationSupportFolder = [self applicationSupportFolder];
90	        NSError *error = nil;
91	        if (![fileManager fileExistsAtPath:applicationSupportFolder isDirectory:NULL]) {
92	            if (![fileManager createDirectoryAtPath:applicationSupportFolder withIntermediateDirectories:NO attributes:nil error:&error]) {
93	                NSAssert(NO, ([NSString stringWithFormat:@"Failed to create App Support directory %@ : %@", applicationSupportFolder, error]));
94	                LOG(@"Error creating application support directory at %@ : %@", applicationSupportFolder, error);
95	                _persistentContainer = nil;
96	                return nil;
97	            }
98	        }
99	        
100	        NSURL *url = [NSURL fileURLWithPath:[applicationSupportFolder stringByAppendingPathComponent:_dataStoreName]];
101	        storeDescription = [NSPersistentStoreDescription persistentStoreDescriptionWithURL:url];
102	    }
103	    
104	    storeDescription.type = _initialType;
105	    storeDescription.shouldMigrateStoreAutomatically = YES;
106	    storeDescription.shouldInferMappingModelAutomatically = YES;
107	    
108	    _persistentContainer.persistentStoreDescriptions = @[storeDescription];
109	    
110	    dispatch_semaphore_t sem = dispatch_semaphore_create(0);
111	    __block NSError *loadError = nil;
112	    
113	    [_persistentContainer loadPersistentStoresWithCompletionHandler:^(NSPersistentStoreDescription *description, NSError *error) {
114	        if (error) {
115	            loadError = error;
116	        }
117	        dispatch_semaphore_signal(sem);
118	    }];
119	    
120	    dispatch_semaphore_wait(sem, DISPATCH_TIME_FOREVER);
121	    
122	    if (loadError) {
123	        if ([loadError code] == 134100) {
124	            if ([[self delegate] respondsToSelector:@selector(coreDataController:encounteredIncorrectModelWithVersionIdentifiers:)]) {
125	                NSError *metadataError = nil;
126	                NSDictionary *metadata = [NSPersistentStoreCoordinator metadataForPersistentStoreOfType:self.initialType URL:storeDescription.URL options:nil error:&metadataError];
127	                if (metadata) {
128	                    [[self delegate] coreDataController:self encounteredIncorrectModelWithVersionIdentifiers:metadata[NSStoreModelVersionIdentifiersKey]];
129	                } else {
130	                    LOG(@"Error retrieving metadata for version identifiers: %@", metadataError);
131	                }
132	            }
133	        } else {
134	            [[NSApplication sharedApplication] presentError:loadError];
135	        }
136	        _persistentContainer = nil;
137	        return nil;
138	    }
139	    
140	    return _persistentContainer;
141	}

146	}

153	- (BOOL)save:(NSError **)error
154	{
155	    BOOL reply = YES;
156		NSManagedObjectContext *moc = [self managedObjectContext];
157		if (moc != nil) {
158			if ([moc commitEditing]) {
159				if ([moc hasChanges]) {
160	                return [moc save:error];
161	            }
162	        }
163		}
164		return reply;
165	}

36	        _contactDataController = [[ContactDataController alloc] initWithCoreDataController:_coreDataController];

51	{

55	- (NSApplicationTerminateReply)applicationShouldTerminate:(NSApplication *)sender
56	{
57	    NSError *error = nil;
58		NSUInteger reply = NSTerminateNow;
59	    BOOL saved = [_coreDataController save:&error];
60	
61	    if (!saved) {
62	        BOOL errorResult = [[NSApplication sharedApplication] presentError:error];
63	        
64	        if (errorResult) {
65	            reply = NSTerminateCancel;
66	        } else {
67	            NSAlert *alert = [[NSAlert alloc] init];
68	            [alert addButtonWithTitle:FCLocalizedString(@"Quit")];
69	            [alert addButtonWithTitle:FCLocalizedString(@"Cancel")];
70	            alert.messageText = @"";
71	            alert.informativeText =  FCLocalizedString(@"QuitQuestion");
72	            NSModalResponse alertReturn = [alert runModal];
73	            if (alertReturn == NSAlertFirstButtonReturn) {
74	                reply = NSTerminateCancel;	
75	            }
76	        }
77	    }
78	    return reply;
79	}

I've now got a clear picture of the app. Here's where it stands:

- **Stack**: Objective-C + AppKit, XIB-based UI, Core Data via `NSPersistentContainer`, Cocoa Bindings/KVO, XCTest suite.
- **Structure**: classic master-detail — `MainWindowController` hosts a `ContactListViewController` (table) + `ContactDetailViewController` (fields).
- **Model**: single `Contact` entity with just `firstName`, `lastName`, `emailAddress`, `phoneNumber`.
- **Toolchain**: Xcode 26.5, macOS 26.5 (Tahoe) SDK, Swift 6.3 — so the "Liquid Glass" Tahoe look is fully available to build against.
- **Workflow**: you've been shipping focused, single-purpose PRs (#1–#8).

The big fork in the road here is *how* we get to a native Tahoe look. That decision changes everything downstream, so let me get your direction before I commit to a plan.

Here's my plan. Since you ship focused PRs, I'll treat this as a roadmap and execute the **foundation PR** now:

**Roadmap**
- **PR A — Foundation (this one):** Convert the target to Swift/SwiftUI + SwiftData on macOS 26. Three-column `NavigationSplitView` (sidebar / list / detail), Liquid Glass toolbar baseline, full CRUD, sample seed data. Remove ObjC/XIB UI + Core Data stack. Replace the ObjC test suite with Swift tests against an in-memory SwiftData container. Get it building and running.
- **PR B — Richer fields:** multiple emails/phones, company/title, address, birthday, notes.
- **PR C — Search & sections:** live search + alphabetical sectioning + sort.
- **PR D — Contact photos:** avatar with initials fallback, photo import, external storage.
- **PR E — Groups & vCard:** sidebar groups/tags, membership, `.vcf` import/export.
- **PR F — Tahoe polish:** Liquid Glass refinements, animations, empty states, keyboard/menu commands.

Let me record the direction in memory and set up the branch.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/Contact.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  Contact.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  The SwiftData model backing a single contact. Replaces the legacy\n//  Core Data `Contact` NSManagedObject.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\n@Model\nfinal class Contact {\n    var firstName: String\n    var lastName: String\n    var emailAddress: String\n    var phoneNumber: String\n    var createdAt: Date\n\n    init(\n        firstName: String = \"\",\n        lastName: String = \"\",\n        emailAddress: String = \"\",\n        phoneNumber: String = \"\",\n        createdAt: Date = .now\n    ) {\n        self.firstName = firstName\n        self.lastName = lastName\n        self.emailAddress = emailAddress\n        self.phoneNumber = phoneNumber\n        self.createdAt = createdAt\n    }\n}\n\nextension Contact {\n    /// Human-readable name, falling back to a placeholder for brand-new contacts.\n    var fullName: String {\n        let name = [firstName, lastName]\n            .map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) }\n            .filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n            .joined(separator: \" \")\n        return name.isEmpty ? \"New Contact\" : name\n    }\n\n    /// One or two uppercase letters used for the avatar placeholder.\n    var initials: String {\n        let first = firstName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).first.map(String.init) ?? \"\"\n        let last = lastName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).first.map(String.init) ?? \"\"\n        let combined = (first + last).uppercased()\n        return combined.isEmpty ? \"#\" : combined\n    }\n\n    /// Lowercased key used to sort contacts by last name, then first name.\n    var sortKey: String {\n        let last = lastName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        let primary = last.isEmpty ? firstName : last\n        return primary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).lowercased()\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/ContactQuery.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactQuery.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Pure, testable helpers for filtering and sorting contacts. Keeping this\n//  logic out of the views makes it straightforward to unit test.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum ContactQuery {\n    /// Sorts contacts by last name, then first name, case-insensitively.\n    static func sorted(_ contacts: [Contact]) -> [Contact] {\n        contacts.sorted { lhs, rhs in\n            if lhs.sortKey != rhs.sortKey {\n                return lhs.sortKey < rhs.sortKey\n            }\n            return lhs.firstName.lowercased() < rhs.firstName.lowercased()\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Filters contacts whose name, email, or phone contains the query.\n    /// An empty query returns every contact unchanged.\n    static func filtered(_ contacts: [Contact], matching query: String) -> [Contact] {\n        let needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()\n        guard !needle.isEmpty else { return contacts }\n\n        return contacts.filter { contact in\n            contact.fullName.lowercased().contains(needle)\n                || contact.emailAddress.lowercased().contains(needle)\n                || contact.phoneNumber.lowercased().contains(needle)\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//\n//  SampleData.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Seeds a fresh store with a few sample contacts so the app has something\n//  to show on first launch.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nenum SampleData {\n    static let contacts: [Contact] = [\n        Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\",\n                emailAddress: \"ada@analytical.engine\", phoneNumber: \"+1 (555) 0100\"),\n        Contact(firstName: \"Alan\", lastName: \"Turing\",\n                emailAddress: \"alan@bletchley.uk\", phoneNumber: \"+44 20 7555 0142\"),\n        Contact(firstName: \"Grace\", lastName: \"Hopper\",\n                emailAddress: \"grace@navy.mil\", phoneNumber: \"+1 (555) 0199\"),\n    ]\n\n    /// Inserts the sample contacts only when the store is empty.\n    @MainActor\n    static func seedIfNeeded(_ context: ModelContext) {\n        let existing = (try? context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<Contact>())) ?? 0\n        guard existing == 0 else { return }\n\n        for contact in contacts {\n            context.insert(contact)\n        }\n        try? context.save()\n    }\n}\n"
}

Owns selection and the create/delete actions.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\nimport SwiftData\n\nstruct ContentView: View {\n    @Environment(\\.modelContext) private var context\n\n    @Query(sort: [SortDescriptor(\\Contact.lastName), SortDescriptor(\\Contact.firstName)])\n    private var contacts: [Contact]\n\n    @State private var sidebarSelection: SidebarItem? = .allContacts\n    @State private var selectedContact: Contact?\n\n    var body: some View {\n        NavigationSplitView {\n            SidebarView(selection: $sidebarSelection, contactCount: contacts.count)\n        } content: {\n            ContactListView(\n                contacts: contacts,\n                selection: $selectedContact,\n                addContact: addContact,\n                deleteContact: deleteContact\n            )\n        } detail: {\n            if let selectedContact {\n                ContactDetailView(contact: selectedContact)\n                    .id(selectedContact.persistentModelID)\n            } else {\n                ContactPlaceholderView()\n            }\n        }\n        .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .newContactRequested)) { _ in\n            addContact()\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Actions\n\n    private func addContact() {\n        let contact = Contact()\n        context.insert(contact)\n        try? context.save()\n        selectedContact = contact\n    }\n\n    private func deleteContact(_ contact: Contact) {\n        if selectedContact?.persistentModelID == contact.persistentModelID {\n            selectedContact = nil\n        }\n        context.delete(contact)\n        try? context.save()\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    ContentView()\n        .modelContainer(for: Contact.self, inMemory: true)\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Views/AvatarView.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  AvatarView.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Circular avatar showing the contact's initials over a tinted gradient.\n//  Photo support arrives in a later milestone; this is the fallback.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct AvatarView: View {\n    let contact: Contact\n    var size: CGFloat = 64\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Circle()\n            .fill(gradient)\n            .overlay {\n                Text(contact.initials)\n                    .font(.system(size: size * 0.4, weight: .semibold, design: .rounded))\n                    .foregroundStyle(.white)\n                    .minimumScaleFactor(0.5)\n            }\n            .frame(width: size, height: size)\n    }\n\n    /// A stable per-contact color so avatars stay visually distinct.\n    private var gradient: LinearGradient {\n        let palette: [Color] = [.blue, .indigo, .teal, .pink, .orange, .purple, .green, .red]\n        let index = abs(contact.initials.hashValue) % palette.count\n        let base = palette[index]\n        return LinearGradient(\n            colors: [base, base.opacity(0.65)],\n            startPoint: .topLeading,\n            endPoint: .bottomTrailing\n        )\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env ruby\n# One-shot migration: convert the ObjC/AppKit ContactManager target into a\n# Swift/SwiftUI + SwiftData app and the test target into a Swift Testing bundle.\n# Run with the xcodeproj gem: `ruby scripts/modernize_project.rb`\n\nrequire \"xcodeproj\"\n\nPROJECT_PATH = \"ContactManager.xcodeproj\"\nproject = Xcodeproj::Project.open(PROJECT_PATH)\n\napp_target  = project.targets.find { |t| t.name == \"ContactManager\" }\ntest_target = project.targets.find { |t| t.name == \"ContactManagerTests\" }\nraise \"targets not found\" unless app_target && test_target\n\n# --- 1. Clear existing source/resource build phases ----------------------------\n[app_target, test_target].each do |t|\n  t.source_build_phase.clear\n  t.resources_build_phase.clear if t.resources_build_phase\nend\n\n# --- 2. Remove legacy ObjC / XIB / Core Data file references -------------------\nremove_names = %w[\n  main.m ContactManager-Prefix.pch\n  ContactManagerAppDelegate.h ContactManagerAppDelegate.m\n  MainWindowController.h MainWindowController.m MainWindowController.xib\n  ContactListViewController.h ContactListViewController.m ContactListViewController.xib\n  ContactDetailViewController.h ContactDetailViewController.m ContactDetailViewController.xib\n  Contact.h Contact.m\n  ContactDataController.h ContactDataController.m\n  CoreDataController.h CoreDataController.m CoreDataControllerDelegate.h\n  NSManagedObjectModel+Extensions.h NSManagedObjectModel+Extensions.m\n  Macros.h ContactManager-Info.plist\n  ContactManagerTests-Info.plist ContactManagerTests-Prefix.pch\n  BaseTestCase.h BaseTestCase.m ContactManagerAppDelegateTests.m\n  ContactDetailViewControllerTests.m ContactListViewControllerKVOTests.m\n  ContactListViewControllerTests.m ContactDataControllerKVOTests.m\n  ContactDataControllerTests.m CoreDataControllerTests.m MainWindowControllerTests.m\n  Credits.rtf MainMenu.xib InfoPlist.strings Localizable.strings\n  ContactManagerModel.xcdatamodeld ContactManagerModel.xcdatamodel\n]\n\nproject.objects.select { |o|\n  %w[PBXFileReference PBXVariantGroup XCVersionGroup].include?(o.isa)\n}.each do |obj|\n  base = (obj.respond_to?(:path) && obj.path) ? File.basename(obj.path) : nil\n  if remove_names.include?(obj.display_name) || (base && remove_names.include?(base))\n    obj.remove_from_project\n  end\nend\n\n# --- 3. Re-add the asset catalog to the app's resources -----------------------\nasset_ref = project.files.find { |f| f.path == \"Images.xcassets\" }\napp_target.resources_build_phase.add_file_reference(asset_ref, true) if asset_ref\n\n# --- 4. Add the new Swift sources ---------------------------------------------\ndef group_at(parent, name)\n  parent[name] || parent.new_group(name, name)\nend\n\ncm_group = project.main_group[\"ContactManager\"]\napp_sources = {\n  \"App\"    => %w[ContactManagerApp.swift],\n  \"Models\" => %w[Contact.swift ContactQuery.swift SampleData.swift],\n  \"Views\"  => %w[ContentView.swift SidebarView.swift ContactListView.swift AvatarView.swift ContactDetailView.swift],\n}\napp_refs = []\napp_sources.each do |subdir, files|\n  grp = group_at(cm_group, subdir)\n  files.each { |f| app_refs << grp.new_file(f) }\nend\napp_target.add_file_references(app_refs)\n\ntests_group = project.main_group[\"ContactManagerTests\"]\ntest_refs = [tests_group.new_file(\"ContactModelTests.swift\")]\ntest_target.add_file_references(test_refs)\n\n# --- 5. Modernize build settings ----------------------------------------------\nDROP = %w[INFOPLIST_FILE GCC_PREFIX_HEADER GCC_PRECOMPILE_PREFIX_HEADER GCC_VERSION]\n\napp_target.build_configurations.each do |config|\n  s = config.build_settings\n  DROP.each { |k| s.delete(k) }\n  s[\"GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE\"] = \"YES\"\n  s[\"SWIFT_VERSION\"] = \"5.0\"\n  s[\"MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET\"] = \"26.0\"\n  s[\"ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME\"] = \"YES\"\n  s[\"SWIFT_EMIT_LOC_STRINGS\"] = \"YES\"\n  s[\"ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME\"] = \"AppIcon\"\n  s[\"REDACTED\"] = \"public.app-category.productivity\"\n  s[\"REDACTED\"] = \"Copyright © 2026 Scott Densmore. All rights reserved.\"\n  s[\"LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS\"] = [\"$(inherited)\", \"@executable_path/../Frameworks\"]\n  s[\"MARKETING_VERSION\"] = \"2.0\"\nend\n\ntest_target.build_configurations.each do |config|\n  s = config.build_settings\n  DROP.each { |k| s.delete(k) }\n  s[\"GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE\"] = \"YES\"\n  s[\"SWIFT_VERSION\"] = \"5.0\"\n  s[\"MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET\"] = \"26.0\"\nend\n\n# --- 6. Project-level housekeeping --------------------------------------------\nproject.build_configurations.each do |config|\n  config.build_settings[\"MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET\"] = \"26.0\"\nend\nproject.root_object.attributes[\"LastUpgradeCheck\"] = \"2650\"\n\nproject.save\nputs \"Project modernized.\"\nputs \"App sources:  #{app_target.source_build_phase.files_references.map(&:display_name).sort.join(', ')}\"\nputs \"Test sources: #{test_target.source_build_phase.files_references.map(&:display_name).sort.join(', ')}\"\n"
}

> AGENT

Root cause found: `SampleData.contacts` is a `static let` holding shared `@Model` instances. The host app (launched as the test host) inserts those same instances into its real store, and the test inserts the *same* instances into its in-memory store — inserting one `@Model` instance into two contexts traps SwiftData (`Trace/BPT trap`).

Two fixes: make sample data a factory that returns fresh instances, and have the app skip real-store work when running under tests.

> TOOL

tool_use Write
id: toolu_019BPaqZ8U8N86fvXrqqvuZi
```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/SampleData.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  SampleData.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Seeds a fresh store with a few sample contacts so the app has something\n//  to show on first launch.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nenum SampleData {\n    /// Number of contacts produced by `makeContacts()`.\n    static let count = 3\n\n    /// Builds a fresh set of sample contacts. Each call returns brand-new\n    /// instances so they can be safely inserted into any model context.\n    static func makeContacts() -> [Contact] {\n        [\n            Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\",\n                    emailAddress: \"ada@analytical.engine\", phoneNumber: \"+1 (555) 0100\"),\n            Contact(firstName: \"Alan\", lastName: \"Turing\",\n                    emailAddress: \"alan@bletchley.uk\", phoneNumber: \"+44 20 7555 0142\"),\n            Contact(firstName: \"Grace\", lastName: \"Hopper\",\n                    emailAddress: \"grace@navy.mil\", phoneNumber: \"+1 (555) 0199\"),\n        ]\n    }\n\n    /// Inserts the sample contacts only when the store is empty.\n    @MainActor\n    static func seedIfNeeded(_ context: ModelContext) {\n        let existing = (try? context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<Contact>())) ?? 0\n        guard existing == 0 else { return }\n\n        for contact in makeContacts() {\n            context.insert(contact)\n        }\n        try? context.save()\n    }\n}\n"
}

Still only `seedingPopulatesAnEmptyStoreOnce` triggers it — the others are collateral from the process dying. The trap is inside SwiftData's model-container setup: Swift Testing runs tests in parallel, and concurrently spinning up multiple `ModelContainer`s for the same `@Model` type races SwiftData's model registration. The fix is to serialize the suite.

No Swift `fatalError` message — it's a raw runtime trap inside SwiftData. Two likely contributors: (1) my `makeContext()` returns `container.mainContext` while the local `container` goes out of scope, and (2) the host app builds a `Contact` container at launch *and* each test builds another. Let me fix both: hold the container for the test's lifetime, and stop the host app from creating a container during tests.

> TOOL

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/README.md",
  "content": "# Contact Manager\n\n**ContactManager** is a native macOS contact manager built with **SwiftUI** and **SwiftData**, targeting the modern macOS Tahoe (macOS 26) look and feel. It is **100% self-contained** with zero third-party dependencies.\n\nThe app was originally an Objective-C / AppKit / Core Data demo and is being rebuilt, in focused increments, into a polished native Tahoe application.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n- **Platform**: macOS 26.0+ (Tahoe)\n- **UI**: SwiftUI — a three-column `NavigationSplitView` (sidebar / contact list / detail) that automatically adopts the Liquid Glass appearance when built against the macOS 26 SDK.\n- **Persistence**: SwiftData (`@Model`, `ModelContainer`, `@Query`), replacing the legacy Core Data stack.\n- **Language**: Swift\n- **Testing**: Swift Testing, backed by an in-memory `ModelContainer`.\n\n### Source layout\n\n```\nContactManager/\n├── App/      ContactManagerApp.swift   – @main entry point, model container, menu commands\n├── Models/   Contact.swift             – the @Model contact entity + derived values\n│             ContactQuery.swift        – pure, testable filter/sort helpers\n│             SampleData.swift          – first-launch seed data\n└── Views/    ContentView.swift         – NavigationSplitView shell + create/delete actions\n              SidebarView.swift         – groups sidebar (All Contacts)\n              ContactListView.swift     – selectable contact list + toolbar\n              ContactDetailView.swift   – editable detail form\n              AvatarView.swift          – initials avatar with a per-contact tint\n```\n\n---\n\n## Features\n\n- Three-column native layout with a Liquid Glass toolbar.\n- Create, edit (inline, autosaving), and delete contacts.\n- Initials-based avatars.\n- Sample contacts seeded on first launch.\n\n### Roadmap\n\nShipped as small, single-purpose PRs:\n\n1. ✅ **Foundation** — SwiftUI + SwiftData rewrite, CRUD, project modernized to macOS 26.\n2. **Richer fields** — multiple emails/phones, company/title, address, birthday, notes.\n3. **Search & sections** — live search and alphabetical sectioning.\n4. **Contact photos** — photo import with initials fallback.\n5. **Groups & vCard** — user groups/tags and `.vcf` import/export.\n6. **Tahoe polish** — Liquid Glass refinements, animations, and richer empty states.\n\n---\n\n## Getting Started\n\n### Prerequisites\n\nXcode 26 or later (macOS 26 SDK). No dependency managers required.\n\n### Building & Running\n\nOpen `ContactManager.xcodeproj` in Xcode, select the **ContactManager** scheme, and press `Cmd + R`.\n\n### Running the Test Suite\n\n```shell\nxcodebuild -project ContactManager.xcodeproj -scheme ContactManager -destination 'platform=macOS' test\n```\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/ContactField.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactField.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  A labeled, repeatable value (email or phone) belonging to a contact.\n//  Modeled as its own SwiftData entity so a contact can have any number of\n//  them, each with its own label.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nenum FieldKind: String, Codable, CaseIterable {\n    case email\n    case phone\n}\n\nenum FieldLabel: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Identifiable {\n    case home\n    case work\n    case mobile\n    case main\n    case other\n\n    var id: String { rawValue }\n    var title: String { rawValue.capitalized }\n}\n\n@Model\nfinal class ContactField {\n    var kind: FieldKind\n    var label: FieldLabel\n    var value: String\n    /// Preserves the order fields were added within their kind.\n    var sortIndex: Int\n    var contact: Contact?\n\n    init(\n        kind: FieldKind,\n        label: FieldLabel = .home,\n        value: String = \"\",\n        sortIndex: Int = 0\n    ) {\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.label = label\n        self.value = value\n        self.sortIndex = sortIndex\n    }\n}\n\nextension FieldKind {\n    /// Sensible default label when adding a new field of this kind.\n    var defaultLabel: FieldLabel {\n        switch self {\n        case .email: return .home\n        case .phone: return .mobile\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//\n//  Contact.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  The SwiftData model backing a single contact.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\n@Model\nfinal class Contact {\n    // Identity\n    var firstName: String\n    var lastName: String\n\n    // Work\n    var company: String\n    var jobTitle: String\n\n    // Postal address\n    var street: String\n    var city: String\n    var state: String\n    var postalCode: String\n    var country: String\n\n    // Misc\n    var birthday: Date?\n    var notes: String\n    var createdAt: Date\n\n    // Labeled emails and phone numbers.\n    @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \\ContactField.contact)\n    var fields: [ContactField]\n\n    init(\n        firstName: String = \"\",\n        lastName: String = \"\",\n        company: String = \"\",\n        jobTitle: String = \"\",\n        street: String = \"\",\n        city: String = \"\",\n        state: String = \"\",\n        postalCode: String = \"\",\n        country: String = \"\",\n        birthday: Date? = nil,\n        notes: String = \"\",\n        createdAt: Date = .now\n    ) {\n        self.firstName = firstName\n        self.lastName = lastName\n        self.company = company\n        self.jobTitle = jobTitle\n        self.street = street\n        self.city = city\n        self.state = state\n        self.postalCode = postalCode\n        self.country = country\n        self.birthday = birthday\n        self.notes = notes\n        self.createdAt = createdAt\n        self.fields = []\n    }\n}\n\nextension Contact {\n    /// Human-readable name, falling back to company, then a placeholder.\n    var fullName: String {\n        let name = [firstName, lastName]\n            .map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) }\n            .filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n            .joined(separator: \" \")\n        if !name.isEmpty { return name }\n        let trimmedCompany = company.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        return trimmedCompany.isEmpty ? \"New Contact\" : trimmedCompany\n    }\n\n    /// One or two uppercase letters used for the avatar placeholder.\n    var initials: String {\n        let first = firstName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).first.map(String.init) ?? \"\"\n        let last = lastName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).first.map(String.init) ?? \"\"\n        var combined = (first + last).uppercased()\n        if combined.isEmpty {\n            combined = company.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).first.map { String($0).uppercased() } ?? \"\"\n        }\n        return combined.isEmpty ? \"#\" : combined\n    }\n\n    /// Lowercased key used to sort contacts by last name, then first name.\n    var sortKey: String {\n        let last = lastName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        let primary = last.isEmpty ? firstName : last\n        return primary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).lowercased()\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Field helpers\n\n    var emails: [ContactField] { fields(of: .email) }\n    var phones: [ContactField] { fields(of: .phone) }\n\n    func fields(of kind: FieldKind) -> [ContactField] {\n        fields\n            .filter { $0.kind == kind }\n            .sorted { $0.sortIndex < $1.sortIndex }\n    }\n\n    /// The first non-empty email, used as the list subtitle.\n    var primaryEmail: String? {\n        emails.first { !$0.value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty }?.value\n    }\n\n    /// The first non-empty phone number.\n    var primaryPhone: String? {\n        phones.first { !$0.value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty }?.value\n    }\n\n    /// Best available secondary line for list rows: email, then phone, then company.\n    var subtitle: String? {\n        if let email = primaryEmail { return email }\n        if let phone = primaryPhone { return phone }\n        let trimmedCompany = company.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        return trimmedCompany.isEmpty ? nil : trimmedCompany\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/SampleData.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  SampleData.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Seeds a fresh store with a few sample contacts so the app has something\n//  to show on first launch.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nenum SampleData {\n    /// Number of contacts produced by `makeContacts()`.\n    static let count = 3\n\n    /// Builds a fresh set of sample contacts. Each call returns brand-new\n    /// instances so they can be safely inserted into any model context.\n    static func makeContacts() -> [Contact] {\n        let ada = Contact(\n            firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\",\n            company: \"Analytical Engine Co.\", jobTitle: \"Mathematician\",\n            city: \"London\", country: \"United Kingdom\",\n            notes: \"First computer programmer.\"\n        )\n        ada.fields = [\n            ContactField(kind: .email, label: .work, value: \"ada@analytical.engine\", sortIndex: 0),\n            ContactField(kind: .phone, label: .mobile, value: \"+1 (555) 0100\", sortIndex: 0),\n        ]\n\n        let alan = Contact(\n            firstName: \"Alan\", lastName: \"Turing\",\n            company: \"Bletchley Park\", jobTitle: \"Cryptanalyst\",\n            city: \"Milton Keynes\", country: \"United Kingdom\"\n        )\n        alan.fields = [\n            ContactField(kind: .email, label: .work, value: \"alan@bletchley.uk\", sortIndex: 0),\n            ContactField(kind: .phone, label: .work, value: \"+44 20 7555 0142\", sortIndex: 0),\n        ]\n\n        let grace = Contact(\n            firstName: \"Grace\", lastName: \"Hopper\",\n            company: \"US Navy\", jobTitle: \"Rear Admiral\",\n            city: \"Arlington\", state: \"VA\", country: \"USA\"\n        )\n        grace.fields = [\n            ContactField(kind: .email, label: .work, value: \"grace@navy.mil\", sortIndex: 0),\n            ContactField(kind: .phone, label: .main, value: \"+1 (555) 0199\", sortIndex: 0),\n        ]\n\n        return [ada, alan, grace]\n    }\n\n    /// Inserts the sample contacts only when the store is empty.\n    @MainActor\n    static func seedIfNeeded(_ context: ModelContext) {\n        let existing = (try? context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<Contact>())) ?? 0\n        guard existing == 0 else { return }\n\n        for contact in makeContacts() {\n            context.insert(contact)\n        }\n        try? context.save()\n    }\n}\n"
}

{

  "content": "//\n//  ContactDetailView.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Trailing column: an editable form bound directly to the SwiftData model.\n//  Edits autosave through the model context.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\nimport SwiftData\n\nstruct ContactDetailView: View {\n    @Environment(\\.modelContext) private var context\n    @Bindable var contact: Contact\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Form {\n            header\n\n            Section(\"Name\") {\n                TextField(\"First Name\", text: $contact.firstName)\n                TextField(\"Last Name\", text: $contact.lastName)\n            }\n\n            Section(\"Work\") {\n                TextField(\"Company\", text: $contact.company)\n                TextField(\"Job Title\", text: $contact.jobTitle)\n            }\n\n            fieldSection(\"Email\", kind: .email, fields: contact.emails)\n            fieldSection(\"Phone\", kind: .phone, fields: contact.phones)\n\n            Section(\"Address\") {\n                TextField(\"Street\", text: $contact.street)\n                TextField(\"City\", text: $contact.city)\n                TextField(\"State / Province\", text: $contact.state)\n                TextField(\"Postal Code\", text: $contact.postalCode)\n                TextField(\"Country\", text: $contact.country)\n            }\n\n            Section(\"Birthday\") {\n                Toggle(\"Has Birthday\", isOn: birthdayEnabled)\n                if contact.birthday != nil {\n                    DatePicker(\"Date\", selection: birthdayValue, displayedComponents: .date)\n                }\n            }\n\n            Section(\"Notes\") {\n                TextField(\"Notes\", text: $contact.notes, axis: .vertical)\n                    .lineLimit(3...10)\n            }\n        }\n        .formStyle(.grouped)\n        .navigationTitle(contact.fullName)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Header\n\n    private var header: some View {\n        Section {\n            HStack(spacing: 16) {\n                AvatarView(contact: contact, size: 72)\n                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {\n                    Text(contact.fullName)\n                        .font(.title2.weight(.semibold))\n                    let role = [contact.jobTitle, contact.company]\n                        .filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n                        .joined(separator: \" · \")\n                    if !role.isEmpty {\n                        Text(role).foregroundStyle(.secondary)\n                    }\n                }\n                Spacer()\n            }\n            .padding(.vertical, 4)\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Repeatable field sections\n\n    @ViewBuilder\n    private func fieldSection(_ title: String, kind: FieldKind, fields: [ContactField]) -> some View {\n        Section(title) {\n            ForEach(fields) { field in\n                ContactFieldRow(field: field)\n            }\n            .onDelete { offsets in\n                delete(offsets, from: fields)\n            }\n\n            Button {\n                addField(kind: kind)\n            } label: {\n                Label(\"Add \\(title)\", systemImage: \"plus.circle.fill\")\n                    .foregroundStyle(.green)\n            }\n            .buttonStyle(.plain)\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Actions\n\n    private func addField(kind: FieldKind) {\n        let field = ContactField(\n            kind: kind,\n            label: kind.defaultLabel,\n            sortIndex: contact.fields(of: kind).count\n        )\n        field.contact = contact\n        context.insert(field)\n        try? context.save()\n    }\n\n    private func delete(_ offsets: IndexSet, from fields: [ContactField]) {\n        for index in offsets {\n            context.delete(fields[index])\n        }\n        try? context.save()\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Birthday bindings\n\n    private var birthdayEnabled: Binding<Bool> {\n        Binding(\n            get: { contact.birthday != nil },\n            set: { contact.birthday = $0 ? (contact.birthday ?? .now) : nil }\n        )\n    }\n\n    private var birthdayValue: Binding<Date> {\n        Binding(\n            get: { contact.birthday ?? .now },\n            set: { contact.birthday = $0 }\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single editable email/phone row: a label picker plus its value.\nprivate struct ContactFieldRow: View {\n    @Bindable var field: ContactField\n\n    var body: some View {\n        HStack {\n            Picker(\"\", selection: $field.label) {\n                ForEach(FieldLabel.allCases) { label in\n                    Text(label.title).tag(label)\n                }\n            }\n            .labelsHidden()\n            .fixedSize()\n\n            TextField(placeholder, text: $field.value)\n                .textContentType(field.kind == .email ? .emailAddress : .telephoneNumber)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private var placeholder: String {\n        field.kind == .email ? \"name@example.com\" : \"Phone\"\n    }\n}\n\nstruct ContactPlaceholderView: View {\n    var body: some View {\n        ContentUnavailableView(\n            \"No Contact Selected\",\n            systemImage: \"person.crop.circle\",\n            description: Text(\"Select a contact to view and edit their details.\")\n        )\n    }\n}\n"
}

Holding it as a stored\n    // property keeps it alive for the lifetime of the test.\n    let container: ModelContainer\n    var context: ModelContext { container.mainContext }\n\n    init() throws {\n        container = try ModelContainer(\n            for: Contact.self, ContactField.self,\n            configurations: ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: true)\n        )\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Persistence\n\n    @Test func insertingContactPersistsIt() throws {\n        context.insert(Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\"))\n        try context.save()\n\n        let fetched = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<Contact>())\n        #expect(fetched.count == 1)\n        #expect(fetched.first?.firstName == \"Ada\")\n    }\n\n    @Test func deletingContactRemovesIt() throws {\n        let contact = Contact(firstName: \"Grace\", lastName: \"Hopper\")\n        context.insert(contact)\n        try context.save()\n\n        context.delete(contact)\n        try context.save()\n\n        #expect(try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<Contact>()) == 0)\n    }\n\n    @Test func deletingContactCascadesToItsFields() throws {\n        let contact = Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\")\n        contact.fields = [\n            ContactField(kind: .email, value: \"ada@analytical.engine\"),\n            ContactField(kind: .phone, value: \"+1 (555) 0100\"),\n        ]\n        context.insert(contact)\n        try context.save()\n        #expect(try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<ContactField>()) == 2)\n\n        context.delete(contact)\n        try context.save()\n        #expect(try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<ContactField>()) == 0)\n    }\n\n    @Test func seedingPopulatesAnEmptyStoreOnce() throws {\n        SampleData.seedIfNeeded(context)\n        #expect(try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<Contact>()) == SampleData.count)\n        #expect(try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<ContactField>()) > 0)\n\n        // Seeding again should be a no-op on a non-empty store.\n        SampleData.seedIfNeeded(context)\n        #expect(try context.fetchCount(FetchDescriptor<Contact>()) == SampleData.count)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Derived values\n\n    @Test func fullNameJoinsAvailablePartsThenFallsBackToCompany() {\n        #expect(Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\").fullName == \"Ada Lovelace\")\n        #expect(Contact(firstName: \"Ada\").fullName == \"Ada\")\n        #expect(Contact(company: \"Acme\").fullName == \"Acme\")\n        #expect(Contact().fullName == \"New Contact\")\n    }\n\n    @Test func initialsUseFirstAndLastInitial() {\n        #expect(Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\").initials == \"AL\")\n        #expect(Contact(firstName: \"grace\").initials == \"G\")\n        #expect(Contact(company: \"acme\").initials == \"A\")\n        #expect(Contact().initials == \"#\")\n    }\n\n    @Test func primaryValuesAndSubtitlePreferEmail() {\n        let contact = Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", company: \"Analytical\")\n        contact.fields = [\n            ContactField(kind: .phone, value: \"+1 (555) 0100\", sortIndex: 0),\n            ContactField(kind: .email, value: \"ada@analytical.engine\", sortIndex: 0),\n        ]\n        #expect(contact.primaryEmail == \"ada@analytical.engine\")\n        #expect(contact.primaryPhone == \"+1 (555) 0100\")\n        #expect(contact.subtitle == \"ada@analytical.engine\")\n\n        let companyOnly = Contact(firstName: \"Bob\", company: \"Globex\")\n        #expect(companyOnly.subtitle == \"Globex\")\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Query helpers\n\n    @Test func sortingOrdersByLastNameThenFirstName() {\n        let contacts = [\n            Contact(firstName: \"Grace\", lastName: \"Hopper\"),\n            Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\"),\n            Contact(firstName: \"Alan\", lastName: \"Turing\"),\n        ]\n        let sorted = ContactQuery.sorted(contacts)\n        #expect(sorted.map(\\.lastName) == [\"Hopper\", \"Lovelace\", \"Turing\"])\n    }\n\n    @Test func filteringMatchesName_Company_Notes_AndFieldValues() throws {\n        let ada = Contact(firstName: \"Ada\", lastName: \"Lovelace\", company: \"Analytical Engine\")\n        ada.fields = [ContactField(kind: .email, value: \"ada@analytical.engine\")]\n        let alan = Contact(firstName: \"Alan\", lastName: \"Turing\", notes: \"Enigma\")\n        alan.fields = [ContactField(kind: .phone, value: \"+44 20 7555 0142\")]\n        context.insert(ada)\n        context.insert(alan)\n        try context.save()\n\n        let all = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<Contact>())\n        #expect(ContactQuery.filtered(all, matching: \"love\").count == 1)        // name\n        #expect(ContactQuery.filtered(all, matching: \"analytical\").count == 1)  // company + email\n        #expect(ContactQuery.filtered(all, matching: \"enigma\").first?.firstName == \"Alan\") // notes\n        #expect(ContactQuery.filtered(all, matching: \"7555\").first?.firstName == \"Alan\")   // phone field\n        #expect(ContactQuery.filtered(all, matching: \"\").count == 2)\n        #expect(ContactQuery.filtered(all, matching: \"nobody\").isEmpty)\n    }\n}\n"

> AGENT

Clear diagnosis: a **fresh store works**, but migrating the PR-A store fails because the new non-optional `String` attributes (`city`, etc.) have no *schema-level* default — they're only defaulted in `init`. SwiftData lightweight migration needs the default on the property declaration to backfill existing rows. That's the proper fix (not a hack): add inline defaults.

34	## Features
35	
36	- Three-column native layout with a Liquid Glass toolbar.

41	### Roadmap
42	
43	Shipped as small, single-purpose PRs:
44	
45	1. ✅ **Foundation** — SwiftUI + SwiftData rewrite, CRUD, project modernized to macOS 26.

47	3. **Search & sections** — live search and alphabetical sectioning.
48	4. **Contact photos** — photo import with initials fallback.
49	5. **Groups & vCard** — user groups/tags and `.vcf` import/export.
50	6. **Tahoe polish** — Liquid Glass refinements, animations, and richer empty states.

==================== PR #9 inline comments ====================
FILE: ContactManager/Views/AvatarView.swift:31
BODY: `contact.initials.hashValue` is not stable across app launches (Swift hashes are seeded per process) and will also change whenever the user edits the name, so the avatar tint won’t be “stable per-contact” as the comment claims. Consider basing the color on a persisted stable identifier (e.g., a UUID property on `Contact`, or `persistentModelID`/`createdAt`) and use a deterministic hash for that value.
---
FILE: ContactManager/Views/AvatarView.swift:31
BODY: `abs(contact.initials.hashValue)` can overflow and trap if the hash happens to be `Int.min`. To avoid a potential crash, use an unsigned/magnitude-based approach (e.g., `contact.initials.hashValue.magnitude`) or convert via `UInt(bitPattern:)` before modulo.
---
FILE: ContactManager/Views/ContentView.swift:51
BODY: `try? context.save()` silently drops persistence errors, which can leave the UI believing a contact was created even if the save failed. Handle the thrown error (e.g., `do/catch` with user-visible error state, and consider rolling back/removing the inserted contact on failure).
---
FILE: ContactManager/Views/ContentView.swift:59
BODY: `try? context.save()` suppresses delete failures; if the save throws, the row may disappear temporarily while the deletion doesn’t actually persist. Please handle the error path (e.g., `do/catch` and restore selection / avoid clearing the selection until the delete+save succeeds).
---
FILE: ContactManager/Models/SampleData.swift:38
BODY: `seedIfNeeded` treats a failed `fetchCount` as if the store were empty (`?? 0`) and also ignores `save()` errors. If `fetchCount` fails due to a store issue, this will attempt to seed anyway and may mask the underlying error. Consider making `seedIfNeeded` throw (or return a Result) and only seed on a successful count of 0, then handle/save errors explicitly.
---
FILE: ContactManager/Models/ContactQuery.swift:19
BODY: The tie-breaker compares `firstName.lowercased()` without trimming whitespace, while `sortKey` trims whitespace. This can produce surprising ordering when names contain leading/trailing spaces. Consider trimming `firstName` (and/or using a dedicated `firstNameSortKey`) for consistency.
---
FILE: ContactManager/App/ContactManagerApp.swift:33
BODY: Crashing the app with `fatalError` on ModelContainer creation failure can lead to a crash loop if the store becomes corrupt or the container can’t be created for environmental reasons. Consider presenting an error state in the UI (and potentially offering a “Reset data” option) instead of terminating the process.
---
==================== PR #10 inline comments ====================
FILE: ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView.swift:112
BODY: Using `contact.fields(of: kind).count` as the next `sortIndex` can create duplicate `sortIndex` values after deletions (e.g., delete index 0, remaining is 1, then count==1 assigns 1 again). This makes ordering unstable when `fields(of:)` sorts by `sortIndex`. Consider assigning `sortIndex` as `(max sortIndex + 1)` for that kind (or renumbering after deletes) to keep a strict insertion order.

---
FILE: ContactManager/Models/ContactQuery.swift:30
BODY: The doc comment above `filtered(_:matching:)` still says it filters by name/email/phone, but the implementation now searches company, job title, notes, and `ContactField.value`. Please update the comment so it matches the current search behavior.
---

1	//
2	//  ContactQuery.swift
3	//  ContactManager
4	//
5	//  Pure, testable helpers for filtering and sorting contacts. Keeping this
6	//  logic out of the views makes it straightforward to unit test.
7	//
8	
9	import Foundation
10	
11	enum ContactQuery {
12	    /// Sorts contacts by last name, then first name, case-insensitively.
13	    static func sorted(_ contacts: [Contact]) -> [Contact] {
14	        contacts.sorted { lhs, rhs in
15	            if lhs.sortKey != rhs.sortKey {
16	                return lhs.sortKey < rhs.sortKey
17	            }
18	            return lhs.firstName.lowercased() < rhs.firstName.lowercased()
19	        }
20	    }
21	
22	    /// Filters contacts whose name, email, or phone contains the query.
23	    /// An empty query returns every contact unchanged.
24	    static func filtered(_ contacts: [Contact], matching query: String) -> [Contact] {
25	        let needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()
26	        guard !needle.isEmpty else { return contacts }
27	
28	        return contacts.filter { contact in
29	            contact.fullName.lowercased().contains(needle)
30	                || contact.emailAddress.lowercased().contains(needle)
31	                || contact.phoneNumber.lowercased().contains(needle)
32	        }
33	    }
34	}
35

//
//  ContactQuery.swift
//  ContactManager
//
//  Pure, testable helpers for filtering and sorting contacts. Keeping this
//  logic out of the views makes it straightforward to unit test.
//

import Foundation

enum ContactQuery {
    /// Sorts contacts by last name, then first name, case-insensitively.
    static func sorted(_ contacts: [Contact]) -> [Contact] {
        contacts.sorted { lhs, rhs in
            if lhs.sortKey != rhs.sortKey {
                return lhs.sortKey < rhs.sortKey
            }
            return lhs.firstNameSortKey < rhs.firstNameSortKey
        }
    }

    /// Filters contacts whose name, email, or phone contains the query.
    /// An empty query returns every contact unchanged.
    static func filtered(_ contacts: [Contact], matching query: String) -> [Contact] {
        let needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()
        guard !needle.isEmpty else { return contacts }

        return contacts.filter { contact in
            let haystacks = [
                contact.fullName,
                contact.company,
                contact.jobTitle,
                contact.notes,
            ] + contact.fields.map(\.value)

            return haystacks.contains { $0.lowercased().contains(needle) }
        }
    }
}

9	import SwiftUI
10	import SwiftData
11	
12	struct ContentView: View {
13	    @Environment(\.modelContext) private var context
14	
15	    @Query(sort: [SortDescriptor(\Contact.lastName), SortDescriptor(\Contact.firstName)])
16	    private var contacts: [Contact]
17	
18	    @State private var sidebarSelection: SidebarItem? = .allContacts
19	    @State private var selectedContact: Contact?
20	    @State private var errorMessage: String?
21	
22	    var body: some View {
23	        NavigationSplitView {
24	            SidebarView(selection: $sidebarSelection, contactCount: contacts.count)
25	        } content: {
26	            ContactListView(
27	                contacts: contacts,
28	                selection: $selectedContact,
29	                addContact: addContact,
30	                deleteContact: deleteContact
31	            )
32	        } detail: {
33	            if let selectedContact {
34	                ContactDetailView(contact: selectedContact)
35	                    .id(selectedContact.persistentModelID)
36	            } else {
37	                ContactPlaceholderView()
38	            }
39	        }
40	        .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .newContactRequested)) { _ in
41	            addContact()
42	        }
43	        .alert(
44	            "Couldn't Save Changes",
45	            isPresented: Binding(get: { errorMessage != nil }, set: { if !$0 { errorMessage = nil } }),
46	            presenting: errorMessage
47	        ) { _ in
48	            Button("OK", role: .cancel) {}
49	        } message: { message in
50	            Text(message)
51	        }
52	    }
53	
54	    // MARK: - Actions
55	
56	    private func addContact() {
57	        let contact = Contact()
58	        context.insert(contact)
59	        do {
60	            try context.save()
61	            selectedContact = contact
62	        } catch {
63	            // Roll back the insert so the UI doesn't show a contact that
64	            // wasn't actually persisted.
65	            context.delete(contact)
66	            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
67	        }
68	    }
69	
70	    private func deleteContact(_ contact: Contact) {
71	        let wasSelected = selectedContact?.persistentModelID == contact.persistentModelID
72	        context.delete(contact)
73	        do {
74	            try context.save()
75	            if wasSelected { selectedContact = nil }
76	        } catch {
77	            // Keep the contact (and selection) if the delete didn't persist.
78	            context.rollback()
79	            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription
80	        }
81	    }
82	}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Models/ContactQuery.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactQuery.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Pure, testable helpers for filtering, sorting, and sectioning contacts.\n//  Keeping this logic out of the views makes it straightforward to unit test.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\n/// The order contacts are sorted and grouped by.\nenum ContactSortOrder: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {\n    case lastName\n    case firstName\n\n    var id: String { rawValue }\n\n    var title: String {\n        switch self {\n        case .lastName: return \"Last Name\"\n        case .firstName: return \"First Name\"\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// An alphabetical group of contacts, titled by initial (\"A\"…\"Z\" or \"#\").\nstruct ContactSection: Identifiable {\n    let title: String\n    let contacts: [Contact]\n    var id: String { title }\n}\n\nenum ContactQuery {\n    /// Sorts contacts by the given order's primary key, then its secondary key.\n    static func sorted(_ contacts: [Contact], by order: ContactSortOrder = .lastName) -> [Contact] {\n        contacts.sorted { lhs, rhs in\n            let l = lhs.sortKeys(for: order)\n            let r = rhs.sortKeys(for: order)\n            if l.primary != r.primary {\n                return l.primary < r.primary\n            }\n            return l.secondary < r.secondary\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Filters contacts whose name, company, job title, notes, or any email/\n    /// phone field value contains the query. An empty query returns every\n    /// contact unchanged.\n    static func filtered(_ contacts: [Contact], matching query: String) -> [Contact] {\n        let needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()\n        guard !needle.isEmpty else { return contacts }\n\n        return contacts.filter { contact in\n            let haystacks = [\n                contact.fullName,\n                contact.company,\n                contact.jobTitle,\n                contact.notes,\n            ] + contact.fields.map(\\.value)\n\n            return haystacks.contains { $0.lowercased().contains(needle) }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Groups contacts into alphabetical sections by their initial, sorted\n    /// within each section. Names that don't start with a letter land in a\n    /// trailing \"#\" section.\n    static func sections(_ contacts: [Contact], by order: ContactSortOrder = .lastName) -> [ContactSection] {\n        let ordered = sorted(contacts, by: order)\n        let grouped = Dictionary(grouping: ordered) { sectionTitle(for: $0, order: order) }\n\n        let titles = grouped.keys.sorted { lhs, rhs in\n            if lhs == \"#\" { return false }   // \"#\" always sorts last\n            if rhs == \"#\" { return true }\n            return lhs < rhs\n        }\n\n        return titles.map { ContactSection(title: $0, contacts: grouped[$0] ?? []) }\n    }\n\n    private static func sectionTitle(for contact: Contact, order: ContactSortOrder) -> String {\n        guard let first = contact.sortKeys(for: order).primary.first, first.isLetter else {\n            return \"#\"\n        }\n        return String(first).uppercased()\n    }\n}\n"
}

This happens because `sortKeys(for:)` ultimately derives from `sortKey`/`firstNameSortKey` and doesn’t fall back to `company` when both first/last names are empty, so section grouping can be inconsistent with what users see in the list.

A small fallback to a normalized company key keeps sorting/sectioning aligned with the displayed name for company-only entries, while still mapping symbol/number-leading companies to “#”.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/ImageProcessing.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ImageProcessing.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Downscales and re-encodes picked images into compact avatar JPEGs so the\n//  store stays lean. Uses ImageIO thumbnails for efficient decoding.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport ImageIO\nimport UniformTypeIdentifiers\n\nenum ImageProcessing {\n    /// Longest edge (in pixels) of a generated avatar.\n    static let maxPixelSize: CGFloat = 512\n\n    /// JPEG compression quality for generated avatars.\n    static let compressionQuality: Double = 0.8\n\n    /// Reads an image file and returns a downscaled avatar JPEG, or `nil` if\n    /// the file isn't a decodable image.\n    static func avatarData(from url: URL) -> Data? {\n        guard let source = CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url as CFURL, nil) else { return nil }\n        return avatarData(from: source)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a downscaled avatar JPEG for the given image data, or `nil` if\n    /// the data isn't a decodable image.\n    static func avatarData(from data: Data) -> Data? {\n        guard let source = CGImageSourceCreateWithData(data as CFData, nil) else { return nil }\n        return avatarData(from: source)\n    }\n\n    private static func avatarData(from source: CGImageSource) -> Data? {\n        let options: [CFString: Any] = [\n            kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true,\n            kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true,\n            kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: maxPixelSize,\n        ]\n        guard let thumbnail = CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex(source, 0, options as CFDictionary) else {\n            return nil\n        }\n\n        let output = NSMutableData()\n        guard let destination = CGImageDestinationCreateWithData(\n            output, UTType.jpeg.identifier as CFString, 1, nil\n        ) else { return nil }\n\n        CGImageDestinationAddImage(\n            destination, thumbnail,\n            [kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality: compressionQuality] as CFDictionary\n        )\n        guard CGImageDestinationFinalize(destination) else { return nil }\n        return output as Data\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Views/AvatarView.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  AvatarView.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Circular avatar: shows the contact's photo when set, otherwise their\n//  initials over a stable per-contact tinted gradient.\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\nimport AppKit\n\nstruct AvatarView: View {\n    let contact: Contact\n    var size: CGFloat = 64\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let data = contact.photoData, let image = NSImage(data: data) {\n                Image(nsImage: image)\n                    .resizable()\n                    .scaledToFill()\n            } else {\n                Circle()\n                    .fill(gradient)\n                    .overlay {\n                        Text(contact.initials)\n                            .font(.system(size: size * 0.4, weight: .semibold, design: .rounded))\n                            .foregroundStyle(.white)\n                            .minimumScaleFactor(0.5)\n                    }\n            }\n        }\n        .frame(width: size, height: size)\n        .clipShape(Circle())\n    }\n\n    /// A stable per-contact color so avatars stay visually distinct.\n    private var gradient: LinearGradient {\n        let palette: [Color] = [.blue, .indigo, .teal, .pink, .orange, .purple, .green, .red]\n        // Wrap into range without `abs`, which can trap on Int.min.\n        let index = ((contact.colorSeed % palette.count) + palette.count) % palette.count\n        let base = palette[index]\n        return LinearGradient(\n            colors: [base, base.opacity(0.65)],\n            startPoint: .topLeading,\n            endPoint: .bottomTrailing\n        )\n    }\n}\n"
}

106	        // Use max+1 (not count) so indices stay strictly increasing even after
107	        // rows are deleted, keeping insertion order stable.
108	        let nextIndex = (contact.fields(of: kind).map(\.sortIndex).max() ?? -1) + 1
109	        let field = ContactField(
110	            kind: kind,
111	            label: kind.defaultLabel,
112	            sortIndex: nextIndex
113	        )
114	        field.contact = contact
115	        context.insert(field)
116	        try? context.save()
117	    }

  "content": "//\n//  ImageProcessingTests.swift\n//  ContactManagerTests\n//\n//  Verifies avatar generation downscales and re-encodes images.\n//\n\nimport Testing\nimport CoreGraphics\nimport ImageIO\nimport UniformTypeIdentifiers\n@testable import ContactManager\n\nstruct ImageProcessingTests {\n\n    /// Encodes a solid-color image of the given size as PNG data.\n    private func makePNG(width: Int, height: Int) throws -> Data {\n        let colorSpace = CGColorSpace(name: CGColorSpace.sRGB)!\n        let context = try #require(CGContext(\n            data: nil, width: width, height: height,\n            bitsPerComponent: 8, bytesPerRow: 0, space: colorSpace,\n            bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.premultipliedLast.rawValue\n        ))\n        context.setFillColor(CGColor(red: 0.2, green: 0.4, blue: 0.8, alpha: 1))\n        context.fill(CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: width, height: height))\n        let image = try #require(context.makeImage())\n\n        let data = NSMutableData()\n        let destination = try #require(CGImageDestinationCreateWithData(\n            data, UTType.png.identifier as CFString, 1, nil\n        ))\n        CGImageDestinationAddImage(destination, image, nil)\n        #expect(CGImageDestinationFinalize(destination))\n        return data as Data\n    }\n\n    private func pixelSize(of data: Data) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int) {\n        let source = try #require(CGImageSourceCreateWithData(data as CFData, nil))\n        let image = try #require(CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(source, 0, nil))\n        return (image.width, image.height)\n    }\n\n    @Test func downscalesImagesLargerThanTheMaxEdge() throws {\n        let input = try makePNG(width: 1024, height: 768)\n        let avatar = try #require(ImageProcessing.avatarData(from: input))\n\n        let size = try pixelSize(of: avatar)\n        #expect(max(size.width, size.height) <= Int(ImageProcessing.maxPixelSize))\n        // Aspect ratio is preserved: 1024x768 → 512x384.\n        #expect(size.width == 512)\n        #expect(size.height == 384)\n    }\n\n    @Test func returnsNilForNonImageData() {\n        let garbage = Data(\"not an image\".utf8)\n        #expect(ImageProcessing.avatarData(from: garbage) == nil)\n    }\n}\n"
}

35	## Features
36	
37	- Three-column native layout with a Liquid Glass toolbar.
38	- Create, edit (inline, autosaving), and delete contacts.
39	- Multiple labeled emails and phone numbers per contact (add/remove inline).
40	- Company, job title, postal address, birthday, and free-form notes.
41	- Live search across name, company, title, notes, and field values.
42	- Alphabetical sections with a first-name / last-name sort toggle.
43	- Initials-based avatars.
44	- Sample contacts seeded on first launch.
45	
46	### Roadmap
47	
48	Shipped as small, single-purpose PRs:
49	
50	1. ✅ **Foundation** — SwiftUI + SwiftData rewrite, CRUD, project modernized to macOS 26.
51	2. ✅ **Richer fields** — multiple emails/phones, company/title, address, birthday, notes.
52	3. ✅ **Search & sections** — live search and alphabetical sectioning.
53	4. **Contact photos** — photo import with initials fallback.
54	5. **Groups & vCard** — user groups/tags and `.vcf` import/export.

FILE: ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView.swift:141
BODY: `importPhoto(from:)` performs security-scoped file access plus image decoding/downscaling synchronously from the `.fileImporter` completion (main thread). For large images this can noticeably block the UI. Consider moving the ImageIO work off the main actor (e.g., `Task.detached` / background queue) and then assign `contact.photoData` + `context.save()` back on `MainActor` once the JPEG data is ready.

---
FILE: ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView.swift:107
BODY: The `.fileImporter` completion currently ignores the `.failure` case and `importPhoto(from:)` silently returns when access/decoding fails. This makes “Choose Photo…” appear to do nothing with no user feedback. Consider handling importer errors and surfacing a lightweight alert/toast (or bubbling an error message up to `ContentView`’s existing alert) when the photo can’t be read/decoded/saved.
---
FILE: ContactManager/Views/ContactDetailView.swift:98
BODY: `photoWell` is an interactive control (a `Menu`), but its accessible name will vary based on the underlying `AvatarView` contents (initials text vs. an unlabeled image). Add an explicit `.accessibilityLabel("Change Photo")` (and optionally a hint) so VoiceOver users consistently understand what this control does.

---
FILE: ContactManager/Views/AvatarView.swift:22
BODY: `AvatarView` constructs `NSImage(data:)` directly inside `body`. In lists, SwiftUI may reevaluate `body` frequently, causing repeated image decoding and extra allocations for each row. Consider caching the decoded image (e.g., via `@State` updated in `onChange(of: contact.photoData)`), or refactoring to an `Image` initializer that avoids repeated decoding work.
---
FILE: ContactManagerTests/ImageProcessingTests.swift:23
BODY: The test helper force-unwraps the sRGB color space (`CGColorSpace(name: …)!`). If that ever fails, the entire test process will crash instead of producing a test failure. Prefer `try #require(...)` (or another non-crashing assertion) to keep failures reported through the test framework.
---
FILE: ContactManager/Models/Contact.swift:33
BODY: `@Attribute(.externalStorage)` is an instruction for SwiftData to store large values externally when appropriate, but it’s not a strict guarantee that the blob is always outside the SQLite file. Consider softening the doc comment (e.g., “Stored externally when possible”) to avoid implying a hard storage guarantee.

---
reviews:
[copilot-pull-request-reviewer] COMMENTED

  "new_string": "    private func handleImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {\n        switch result {\n        case .failure(let error):\n            photoError = error.localizedDescription\n        case .success(let url):\n            // Read the picked file while its security scope is held, then hand\n            // the bytes off; downscaling happens off the main actor below.\n            let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()\n            defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }\n            do {\n                let fileData = try Data(contentsOf: url)\n                processPhoto(fileData)\n            } catch {\n                photoError = error.localizedDescription\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func processPhoto(_ fileData: Data) {\n        Task {\n            // Decode/downscale off the main actor so large images don't block UI.\n            let avatar = await Task.detached { ImageProcessing.avatarData(from: fileData) }.value\n            guard let avatar else {\n                photoError = \"That file couldn't be read as an image.\"\n                return\n            }\n            contact.photoData = avatar\n            do { try context.save() } catch { photoError = error.localizedDescription }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func removePhoto() {\n        contact.photoData = nil\n        try? context.save()\n    }"
}

  "content": "//\n//  ContactGroup.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  A user-defined group/tag that contacts can belong to (many-to-many).\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\n@Model\nfinal class ContactGroup {\n    var name: String = \"\"\n    var createdAt: Date = Date.now\n\n    /// Members of this group. Deleting a group nullifies membership rather\n    /// than deleting the contacts themselves.\n    @Relationship(deleteRule: .nullify, inverse: \\Contact.groups)\n    var contacts: [Contact] = []\n\n    init(name: String = \"\", createdAt: Date = .now) {\n        self.name = name\n        self.createdAt = createdAt\n    }\n}\n\nextension ContactGroup {\n    /// Group name shown in the UI, falling back to a placeholder.\n    var displayName: String {\n        let trimmed = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        return trimmed.isEmpty ? \"Untitled Group\" : trimmed\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
