Here's a curated list, with my honest read on each. I tried to balance "real-Mac-app value", testability in this environment, and effort.

## Hardening / quality
- **A. Undo/Redo via `NSUndoManager`** — wire the context's undo manager to the window, so create/edit/delete and group changes are all undoable. Big "real Mac app" win, modest effort, builds directly on `ContactStore`. Fully testable. *(My pick — see bottom.)*
- **B. Accessibility pass** — audit every interactive control for VoiceOver labels/hints/values, full keyboard navigation, Dynamic Type support. I can do the code work; you'd verify with VoiceOver.
- **C. UI tests via XCUITest** — adds a new test target for real click-through journeys (open app → create contact → enter fields → find duplicates → merge). Slower than unit tests, but extends the safety net to the UI layer.
- **D. Swift 6 strict concurrency** — bump `SWIFT_VERSION` to 6 and clean up the resulting data-race warnings. Future-proofs the codebase. Real risk of churn; useful but not urgent.

## Core features
- **E. macOS **Contacts framework** bridge** — import/export with the system Contacts.app (the canonical Mac contact store). Unlocks Mail/Messages interop. Needs Contacts permission entitlement.
- **F. App Intents + Spotlight indexing** — index contacts in Spotlight; expose "Create Contact" / "Find Contact" / "Open Group" as Shortcuts and Siri intents. Modern Mac integration with a small API surface.
- **G. Drag-and-drop** — drag a contact or selection to Finder to write a `.vcf`, drop a `.vcf` onto the list to import, drop an image onto the avatar. Standard mac behavior; very testable manually.
- **H. Preferences scene** — `Settings { ... }` with default sort, default-group-for-new-contacts, "hide empty fields in detail," and a Restore Defaults. Small but useful.

## Polish & UX
- **I. Multi-window** — `OpenWindowAction` + `WindowGroup(for: PersistentIdentifier.self)` so a contact can open in its own window. Tahoe-native pattern.
- **J. MapKit embed in the inspector** for the contact's address — small, visual, fully verifiable.

## Migration / interop
- **K. CSV import** — frequent migration path from Google/Outlook exports.
- **L. iOS/iPad target sharing the SwiftData schema + ContactStore** — biggest jump in surface, opens the door to iPhone sync via the CloudKit container you'll wire up.

---

## My top pick
**Start with A — Undo/Redo.**

Why: it's a core Mac affordance users will reach for and miss; it lands almost free given our architecture (every `ContactStore` mutation is already atomic), it doesn't need an entitlement or a device, and the journey tests against `ContactStore` make it easy to verify *behavior* (undo a create → store empty; undo a merge → both contacts back). With the inspector and the CloudKit-ready container in place, undo is the missing piece that makes this feel like a real Mac app.

Sketch of what'd land: hook the model context's undo manager into the window scene, add a small `ContactStore.undo()` / `redo()` (or rely on the system Edit ▸ Undo menu), and add a journey test per operation. If you want, I'll start it now.

If you'd rather lean into interop instead, my second pick is **E — macOS Contacts bridge**; third is **F — App Intents/Spotlight**.

50	        let palette: [Color] = [.blue, .indigo, .teal, .pink, .orange, .purple, .green, .red]

52	        let index = ((contact.colorSeed % palette.count) + palette.count) % palette.count

> AGENT

My recommendation is still **E — macOS Contacts framework bridge**: a one-way "Import from System Contacts…" menu item that uses the `Contacts` framework to read the user's existing macOS contact store. It's the single biggest "this is a real Mac app" feature you can add, and it solves the cold-start problem (a brand-new install of ContactManager today has nothing in it).

Tradeoff: needs `NSContactsUsageDescription` in the plist and a runtime permission prompt, and the `Contacts` framework APIs are async/throwing so the import path needs proper error handling. Scope-wise I'd keep PR #1 to **read-only import with permission handling**, leaving write-back to the system store for a follow-up if you ever want it.

Want me to start it, or pick something else? (G drag-and-drop and F App Intents+Spotlight are the other strong ones; H preferences scene is small if you want a quick win.)

62	    private static func loadContainer(resettingStore: Bool = false) -> ContainerLoadState {
63	        // When hosting the unit tests, skip building the app's model container
64	        // entirely so the test target owns the only container in the process.
65	        let isTesting = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] != nil
66	            || NSClassFromString("XCTestCase") != nil
67	        if isTesting { return .testing }
68	
69	        if resettingStore {
70	            deleteDefaultStore()
71	        }
72	
73	        // Build a CloudKit-backed container when the iCloud capability is
74	        // present, and fall back to a local-only container otherwise so the
75	        // app still runs without iCloud.
76	        let schema = Schema([Contact.self, ContactField.self, ContactGroup.self])
77	
78	        let container: ModelContainer
79	        var isLocalOnlyFallback = false
80	        do {
81	            // `.automatic` uses the project's iCloud container when an iCloud
82	            // entitlement is present; without one it still loads successfully
83	            // and behaves as a local-only store.
84	            let cloudConfiguration = ModelConfiguration(schema: schema, cloudKitDatabase: .automatic)
85	            container = try ModelContainer(for: schema, configurations: cloudConfiguration)
86	        } catch {
87	            print("ContactManager: CloudKit container failed (\(error.localizedDescription)); using local.")
88	            do {
89	                let localConfiguration = ModelConfiguration(schema: schema, cloudKitDatabase: .none)
90	                container = try ModelContainer(for: schema, configurations: localConfiguration)
91	                isLocalOnlyFallback = true
92	            } catch {
93	                return .failed(error.localizedDescription)
94	            }
95	        }
96	
97	        // Only seed sample data on the confirmed local-only fallback. On a
98	        // CloudKit-capable container the user's real contacts might be about
99	        // to sync down (a fresh install on a second device); seeding then
100	        // would race the sync and propagate the samples to every device.
101	        if isLocalOnlyFallback {
102	            do {
103	                try SampleData.seedIfNeeded(container.mainContext)
104	            } catch {
105	                print("ContactManager: sample data seeding skipped — \(error)")
106	            }
107	        }
108	        return .ready(container)
109	    }
110	
111	    /// Removes the default SwiftData store files so a corrupt store can be
112	    /// recovered from without reinstalling the app.
113	    private static func deleteDefaultStore() {
114	        let fileManager = FileManager.default
115	        guard let support = try? fileManager.url(
116	            for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask,
117	            appropriateFor: nil, create: false
118	        ) else { return }
119	
120	        for suffix in ["", "-wal", "-shm"] {
121	            try? fileManager.removeItem(at: support.appending(path: "default.store\(suffix)"))
122	        }
123	    }
124	}

//
//  ContactGroup.swift
//  ContactManager
//
//  A user-defined group/tag that contacts can belong to (many-to-many).
//

import Foundation
import SwiftData

@Model
final class ContactGroup {
    var name: String = ""
    var createdAt: Date = Date.now

    /// Members of this group. Deleting a group nullifies membership rather
    /// than deleting the contacts themselves.
    @Relationship(deleteRule: .nullify, inverse: \Contact.groups)
    var contacts: [Contact] = []

    init(name: String = "", createdAt: Date = .now) {
        self.name = name
        self.createdAt = createdAt
    }
}

extension ContactGroup {
    /// Group name shown in the UI, falling back to a placeholder.
    var displayName: String {
        let trimmed = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
        return trimmed.isEmpty ? "Untitled Group" : trimmed
    }
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/PersistentIdentifierEncoding.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  PersistentIdentifierEncoding.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  `PersistentIdentifier` is `Codable` but not directly storable in\n//  `@AppStorage` (which only takes a handful of property-list types).\n//  These helpers round-trip a PID through a JSON string so a preference\n//  can point at a SwiftData model without depending on a mutable display\n//  name.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nextension PersistentIdentifier {\n    /// JSON-encoded string suitable for `@AppStorage`. Returns `nil` only\n    /// if encoding unexpectedly fails (shouldn't in practice).\n    var storedString: String? {\n        guard let data = try? JSONEncoder().encode(self) else { return nil }\n        return String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)\n    }\n\n    /// Inverse of `storedString`. Returns `nil` for the empty string (the\n    /// \"no value\" sentinel) or any string that isn't a valid encoded PID.\n    static func decode(stored string: String) -> PersistentIdentifier? {\n        guard !string.isEmpty,\n              let data = string.data(using: .utf8),\n              let id = try? JSONDecoder().decode(PersistentIdentifier.self, from: data)\n        else { return nil }\n        return id\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Views/SettingsView.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  SettingsView.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  The macOS Settings scene (ContactManager ▸ Settings…, ⌘,). All values\n//  are persisted via `@AppStorage` and read directly by the views that\n//  care, so changes apply live without any plumbing.\n//\n\nimport SwiftData\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct SettingsView: View {\n    @AppStorage(\"contactSortOrder\") private var sortOrder: ContactSortOrder = .lastName\n    /// JSON-encoded `PersistentIdentifier` of the default group, or \"\" for\n    /// \"no group\". Storing the PID (not the group's name) means renaming the\n    /// group keeps the preference pointed at the right model and avoids\n    /// ambiguity when two groups share a name.\n    @AppStorage(\"defaultGroupID\") private var defaultGroupID: String = \"\"\n\n    @Query(sort: \\ContactGroup.name) private var groups: [ContactGroup]\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Form {\n            Section(\"Defaults\") {\n                Picker(\"Sort Contacts By\", selection: $sortOrder) {\n                    ForEach(ContactSortOrder.allCases) { order in\n                        Text(order.title).tag(order)\n                    }\n                }\n\n                Picker(\"New Contact Joins\", selection: $defaultGroupID) {\n                    Text(\"No Group\").tag(\"\")\n                    if !groups.isEmpty {\n                        Divider()\n                        ForEach(groups) { group in\n                            Text(group.displayName)\n                                .tag(group.persistentModelID.storedString ?? \"\")\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                .help(\"When the sidebar is on All Contacts, new contacts join this group.\")\n            }\n\n            Section {\n                Button(\"Restore Defaults\", role: .destructive) {\n                    sortOrder = .lastName\n                    defaultGroupID = \"\"\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        .formStyle(.grouped)\n        .frame(width: 440, height: 240)\n        // Prune the preference if its target group was renamed (the encoded\n        // PID stays valid) or deleted (the lookup now misses) — keeps the\n        // picker's selection consistent with what's actually on disk.\n        .onChange(of: groups) { _, _ in pruneStaleDefaultGroup() }\n        .onAppear { pruneStaleDefaultGroup() }\n    }\n\n    private func pruneStaleDefaultGroup() {\n        guard !defaultGroupID.isEmpty,\n              let id = PersistentIdentifier.decode(stored: defaultGroupID)\n        else {\n            if !defaultGroupID.isEmpty { defaultGroupID = \"\" }\n            return\n        }\n        if !groups.contains(where: { $0.persistentModelID == id }) {\n            defaultGroupID = \"\"\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

All three Copilot points addressed in commit `ceb5b5a`:

1. **Stale `defaultGroupName` after rename/delete** → switched the storage to a JSON-encoded `PersistentIdentifier`, so renames don't break the pointer. SettingsView now prunes the preference on appear and whenever the groups list changes.
2. **Group-name collisions** → PIDs are unique, so two groups can share a display name without the picker tags colliding.
3. **Silent fallback on a stale sidebar `.group(...)`** → introduced `groupForNewContact` that switches on `sidebarSelection` explicitly. The default group is only used on `.allContacts` / `.none`; a deleted `.group(...)` selection now creates a groupless contact instead of quietly diverting into the default.

Helper extension lives in `ContactManager/Support/PersistentIdentifierEncoding.swift`. CI green. Ready to merge.

What is next?

> AGENT

Still **E — macOS Contacts framework bridge**. It's the most impactful feature left and solves the cold-start problem: today a fresh install has no contacts unless the user imports a vCard, but every Mac user already has their contacts in the system store. A one-way "Import from System Contacts…" menu item is a focused PR.

Tradeoff: needs `NSContactsUsageDescription` in `Info.plist` (currently generated, so this is a build-setting edit) and a runtime permission prompt; the import has to map system fields to our schema (labels can be arbitrary `CNLabelKey`s, photos come as `Data`). Read-only import keeps the scope tight; write-back can be a follow-up.

Want me to start it, or pick something else? G (drag-and-drop) and K (CSV import) are the other genuinely useful ones; D (Swift 6 strict concurrency) is a future-proofing pass with no user-facing change.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/ContactsBridge.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactsBridge.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Reads contacts from the user's macOS Contacts (Address Book) store via\n//  the `Contacts` framework and maps them to our own `ParsedContact`\n//  values so import flows through the same path as vCard import.\n//\n//  The fetch + mapping pipeline is pure (no SwiftData), so it's testable\n//  with `CNMutableContact` fixtures.\n//\n\nimport Contacts\nimport Foundation\n\nenum ContactsBridge {\n    /// Errors surfaced to the user. Anything else (e.g. an unexpected\n    /// `CNError`) is rethrown so the caller can show its message.\n    enum AccessError: LocalizedError {\n        case denied\n        case restricted\n\n        var errorDescription: String? {\n            switch self {\n            case .denied:\n                \"ContactManager doesn't have permission to read your Contacts. \" +\n                    \"Enable it in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Contacts.\"\n            case .restricted:\n                \"Access to Contacts is restricted on this Mac.\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Keys we need from each unified contact. Listed once so a future\n    /// addition (e.g. notes) is a one-line change.\n    private static let keysToFetch: [CNKeyDescriptor] = [\n        CNContactGivenNameKey, CNContactFamilyNameKey,\n        CNContactOrganizationNameKey, CNContactJobTitleKey,\n        CNContactEmailAddressesKey, CNContactPhoneNumbersKey,\n        CNContactPostalAddressesKey, CNContactBirthdayKey,\n        CNContactImageDataKey,\n    ].map { $0 as CNKeyDescriptor }\n\n    /// Requests permission if needed and returns the unified contact list\n    /// mapped to `ParsedContact`. Safe to call off the main actor.\n    static func fetchAllParsed() async throws -> [ParsedContact] {\n        let store = CNContactStore()\n        try await ensureAccess(store: store)\n\n        let request = CNContactFetchRequest(keysToFetch: keysToFetch)\n        var parsed: [ParsedContact] = []\n        try store.enumerateContacts(with: request) { cnContact, _ in\n            parsed.append(self.parsed(from: cnContact))\n        }\n        return parsed\n    }\n\n    private static func ensureAccess(store: CNContactStore) async throws {\n        switch CNContactStore.authorizationStatus(for: .contacts) {\n        case .authorized: return\n        case .denied: throw AccessError.denied\n        case .restricted: throw AccessError.restricted\n        case .notDetermined:\n            let granted = try await store.requestAccess(for: .contacts)\n            if !granted { throw AccessError.denied }\n        @unknown default:\n            throw AccessError.denied\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Mapping (pure)\n\n    /// Translates a `CNContact` to our `ParsedContact`. Visible for tests.\n    static func parsed(from cnContact: CNContact) -> ParsedContact {\n        var parsed = ParsedContact(\n            firstName: cnContact.givenName,\n            lastName: cnContact.familyName,\n            company: cnContact.organizationName,\n            jobTitle: cnContact.jobTitle\n        )\n        if let birthday = cnContact.birthday {\n            parsed.birthday = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian).date(from: birthday)\n        }\n        if let primary = cnContact.postalAddresses.first?.value {\n            parsed.street = primary.street\n            parsed.city = primary.city\n            parsed.state = primary.state\n            parsed.postalCode = primary.postalCode\n            parsed.country = primary.country\n        }\n        parsed.emails = cnContact.emailAddresses.map { entry in\n            (label: emailLabel(from: entry.label), value: entry.value as String)\n        }\n        parsed.phones = cnContact.phoneNumbers.map { entry in\n            (label: phoneLabel(from: entry.label), value: entry.value.stringValue)\n        }\n        parsed.photoData = cnContact.imageData\n        return parsed\n    }\n\n    private static func emailLabel(from raw: String?) -> FieldLabel {\n        switch raw {\n        case CNLabelHome: .home\n        case CNLabelWork: .work\n        case CNLabelOther: .other\n        default: .other\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static func phoneLabel(from raw: String?) -> FieldLabel {\n        switch raw {\n        case CNLabelPhoneNumberMobile, CNLabelPhoneNumberiPhone: .mobile\n        case CNLabelPhoneNumberMain: .main\n        case CNLabelHome: .home\n        case CNLabelWork: .work\n        case CNLabelPhoneNumberOtherFax, CNLabelOther: .other\n        default: .other\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

CI green. Three fixes in commit `1da3c16`:

1. **Copilot `.limited` handling** → `case .authorized, .limited: return`. `.limited` is the macOS 15+ "user granted access to a subset" status; `enumerateContacts` returns just that subset, which is the right behavior.
2. **Copilot postal-address test gap** → previous fixture left `state = ""`, so the new `parsed.state = primary.state` line could regress silently. New fixture has all five fields populated and each is asserted.
3. **CI lint failure (caught only on CI, not local)** → `cn` is shorter than SwiftLint's `identifier_name` minimum of 3 (CI runs `--strict`, local `make lint` doesn't). Renamed to `cnContact`.

Side note: `make lint` runs without `--strict` locally, which is why this slipped through. If you want them to match, that's a one-line Makefile change — say the word and I'll do it in a follow-up.

Ready to merge.

> AGENT

My pick is **G — Drag-and-drop**. Three concrete affordances Mac users expect that ride on infrastructure you already have:

- **Drag a contact (or selection) to Finder** → writes a `.vcf` file (reuses `VCard.makeDocument` / `VCardDocument`).
- **Drop a `.vcf` onto the contact list** → imports it (reuses the existing `handleImport` path).
- **Drop an image onto the avatar well** → sets the photo (reuses `ImageProcessing.avatarData`).

Tradeoff: SwiftUI's `Transferable` protocol is the modern API on macOS 26 and works well for file-based payloads, but multi-select drag from `List` has historically been finicky — I'd scope the first PR to single-contact drag and add multi-select if it falls out cleanly. No entitlements, no permissions, no schema changes.

Want me to start it, or pick something else? (F App Intents+Spotlight, K CSV import, and I multi-window are the other strong ones.)

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/VCardTransfer.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  VCardTransfer.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  A `Transferable` wrapping a single contact's vCard payload + suggested\n//  filename. Dragging a row hands one of these to Finder, which receives\n//  a `.vcf` file named after the contact.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftUI\nimport UniformTypeIdentifiers\n\nstruct VCardTransfer: Transferable {\n    /// File-system-safe stem, without the `.vcf` extension. Computed by\n    /// `suggestedFilename(for:)` so the sanitization is testable.\n    let suggestedName: String\n    /// The vCard 3.0 text the file will contain.\n    let text: String\n\n    static var transferRepresentation: some TransferRepresentation {\n        FileRepresentation(exportedContentType: .vCard) { transfer in\n            // Write to a per-drag tempdir so multiple drags don't collide on\n            // a shared filename. Finder copies the file out by the time the\n            // OS clears the temp dir at next launch.\n            let directory = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory\n                .appending(path: \"vcard-drag-\\(UUID().uuidString)\")\n            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(\n                at: directory, withIntermediateDirectories: true\n            )\n            let url = directory.appending(path: \"\\(transfer.suggestedName).vcf\")\n            try Data(transfer.text.utf8).write(to: url)\n            return SentTransferredFile(url, allowAccessingOriginalFile: false)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Pure helper: produces a filename stem (\"Ada Lovelace\") from the\n    /// contact's `fullName`, falling back to \"Contact\" for an unnamed one\n    /// and stripping characters that are illegal on macOS file systems.\n    static func suggestedFilename(for displayName: String) -> String {\n        let trimmed = displayName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        let base = trimmed.isEmpty ? \"Contact\" : trimmed\n        // Forward slash and colon are the only path-illegal characters on\n        // HFS+/APFS; replace them rather than dropping them so two distinct\n        // names don't collapse into one.\n        return base\n            .replacingOccurrences(of: \"/\", with: \"-\")\n            .replacingOccurrences(of: \":\", with: \"-\")\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "struct ContactListView: View {\n    let sections: [ContactSection]\n    let totalCount: Int\n    @Binding var searchText: String\n    @Binding var sortOrder: ContactSortOrder\n    @Binding var selection: Contact?\n    var addContact: () -> Void\n    var deleteContact: (Contact) -> Void\n    /// Called when a `.vcf` file is dropped onto the list from Finder.\n    var importVCardURLs: ([URL]) -> Void\n\n    var body: some View {\n        List(selection: $selection) {\n            ForEach(sections) { section in\n                Section(section.title) {\n                    ForEach(section.contacts) { contact in\n                        ContactRow(contact: contact)\n                            .tag(contact)\n                            // Drag a row to Finder to write `<Name>.vcf`.\n                            .draggable(transfer(for: contact))\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        .navigationTitle(\"Contacts\")\n        .navigationSplitViewColumnWidth(\n            min: LayoutMetrics.listMinWidth,\n            ideal: LayoutMetrics.listIdealWidth,\n            max: LayoutMetrics.listMaxWidth\n        )\n        .animation(.smooth, value: sortOrder)\n        .searchable(text: $searchText, prompt: \"Search Contacts\")\n        .overlay { emptyState }\n        // Accept `.vcf` drops from Finder. Filtering on extension keeps\n        // arbitrary file drops from triggering a no-op import.\n        .dropDestination(for: URL.self) { urls, _ in\n            let vcards = urls.filter { $0.pathExtension.lowercased() == \"vcf\" }\n            guard !vcards.isEmpty else { return false }\n            importVCardURLs(vcards)\n            return true\n        }\n        .onDeleteCommand {\n            if let selection { deleteContact(selection) }\n        }"

Data(contentsOf: url),\n                          let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)\n                    else { continue }\n                    all.append(contentsOf: VCard.parse(text))\n                }\n                return all\n            }.value\n\n            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {\n                errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in that file.\"\n                return\n            }\n            do {\n                try store.importContacts(parsed)\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func handleImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {"

What is next?

> AGENT

My pick is **F — App Intents + Spotlight indexing**. Two complementary wins:

- **Spotlight**: typing a contact's name in Spotlight surfaces them; hit return → ContactManager opens with that contact selected.
- **App Intents / Shortcuts**: "Open Contact", "Find Contact", "Create Contact" exposed as Shortcuts actions and Siri intents.

The reason to do them together: the modern Apple pattern is a single `AppEntity` that conforms to `IndexedEntity`, which makes the entity both Shortcuts-addressable and Spotlight-indexable. Splitting them into two PRs means writing the entity twice. Tradeoff: it's a bigger PR (entity definition + intent boilerplate + Spotlight index sync on contact mutations), but no entitlements or runtime permissions.

Want me to start it, or pick something else? (K CSV import and I multi-window are the other strong ones if you want a smaller scope.)

  "content": "//\n//  ContactEntity.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  The App Intents identity for a `Contact`. Conforms to `IndexedEntity`\n//  so the same value also drives the CoreSpotlight attribute set,\n//  avoiding a parallel \"Spotlight model\" alongside the intents model.\n//\n\nimport AppIntents\nimport CoreSpotlight\nimport Foundation\n\nstruct ContactEntity: AppEntity, IndexedEntity {\n    static let typeDisplayRepresentation = TypeDisplayRepresentation(name: \"Contact\")\n    static let defaultQuery = ContactEntityQuery()\n\n    /// Stable identifier: the contact's `PersistentIdentifier` encoded as\n    /// a string (same scheme used by the default-group preference).\n    var id: String\n    var displayName: String\n    var company: String\n    var jobTitle: String\n    var emails: [String]\n    var phones: [String]\n\n    var displayRepresentation: DisplayRepresentation {\n        DisplayRepresentation(\n            title: \"\\(displayName)\",\n            subtitle: subtitleText.map { \"\\($0)\" }\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// CoreSpotlight metadata built from the same fields the entity carries,\n    /// so Spotlight's preview shows the same info Shortcuts/Siri reads.\n    var attributeSet: CSSearchableItemAttributeSet {\n        let attrs = CSSearchableItemAttributeSet(contentType: .contact)\n        attrs.displayName = displayName\n        attrs.contentDescription = subtitleText\n        if !emails.isEmpty { attrs.emailAddresses = emails }\n        if !phones.isEmpty { attrs.phoneNumbers = phones }\n        if !company.isEmpty { attrs.organizations = [company] }\n        if !jobTitle.isEmpty { attrs.title = jobTitle }\n        return attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Subtitle preferences match the contact list row: primary email, then\n    /// primary phone, then company. Returns `nil` if everything is empty.\n    private var subtitleText: String? {\n        if let first = emails.first, !first.isEmpty { return first }\n        if let first = phones.first, !first.isEmpty { return first }\n        if !company.isEmpty { return company }\n        return nil\n    }\n}\n\nextension ContactEntity {\n    /// Snapshot a SwiftData `Contact` into an entity value. Safe to call\n    /// off the main actor as long as the `Contact` is fetched there too.\n    init(contact: Contact) {\n        self.id = contact.persistentModelID.storedString ?? \"\"\n        self.displayName = contact.fullName\n        self.company = contact.company\n        self.jobTitle = contact.jobTitle\n        self.emails = contact.emails.map(\\.value).filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n        self.phones = contact.phones.map(\\.value).filter { !$0.isEmpty }\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Intents/ContactEntityQuery.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  ContactEntityQuery.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Lookup paths for `ContactEntity`: by id (Shortcuts handoff + Spotlight\n//  open), by free-text string (Find Contact intent), and \"all\" (Spotlight\n//  re-index and the Shortcuts picker).\n//\n\nimport AppIntents\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftData\n\nstruct ContactEntityQuery: EntityQuery, EnumerableEntityQuery, EntityStringQuery {\n    func entities(for identifiers: [ContactEntity.ID]) async throws -> [ContactEntity] {\n        guard let container = EntityModelContainer.shared else { return [] }\n        let wanted = Set(identifiers)\n        return try await Self.snapshot(container: container) { contacts in\n            contacts.filter { wanted.contains($0.persistentModelID.storedString ?? \"\") }\n        }\n    }\n\n    func entities(matching string: String) async throws -> [ContactEntity] {\n        guard let container = EntityModelContainer.shared else { return [] }\n        let needle = string.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        guard !needle.isEmpty else { return [] }\n        return try await Self.snapshot(container: container) { contacts in\n            // Reuse the same matcher the contact list uses so Shortcuts and\n            // in-app search behave the same.\n            ContactQuery.filtered(contacts, matching: needle)\n        }\n    }\n\n    func suggestedEntities() async throws -> [ContactEntity] {\n        try await allEntities()\n    }\n\n    func allEntities() async throws -> [ContactEntity] {\n        guard let container = EntityModelContainer.shared else { return [] }\n        return try await Self.snapshot(container: container) { $0 }\n    }\n\n    /// Fetches every contact on a fresh background context, applies the\n    /// caller's filter, and maps to entity values. The fetch and the\n    /// mapping both happen on the same actor as the context (none here),\n    /// so the resulting `[ContactEntity]` is safe to send to App Intents\n    /// callers on any actor.\n    private static func snapshot(\n        container: ModelContainer,\n        filter: (_ contacts: [Contact]) -> [Contact]\n    ) async throws -> [ContactEntity] {\n        let context = ModelContext(container)\n        let descriptor = FetchDescriptor<Contact>(\n            sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\\.lastName), SortDescriptor(\\.firstName)]\n        )\n        let contacts = try context.fetch(descriptor)\n        return filter(contacts).map(ContactEntity.init(contact:))\n    }\n}\n"
}

The actual navigation is handled by `ContentView`\n//  observing `Notification.Name.openContactRequested`.\n//\n\nimport AppIntents\nimport Foundation\n\nstruct OpenContactIntent: AppIntent {\n    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = \"Open Contact\"\n    static let description = IntentDescription(\n        \"Opens ContactManager and selects the chosen contact.\"\n    )\n    /// Tells the system to launch the app for us before `perform()` runs.\n    static let openAppWhenRun = true\n\n    @Parameter(title: \"Contact\") var target: ContactEntity\n\n    @MainActor\n    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {\n        NotificationCenter.default.post(\n            name: .openContactRequested,\n            object: nil,\n            userInfo: [\"id\": target.id]\n        )\n        return .result()\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//\n//  FindContactIntent.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Shortcut/Siri action: returns contacts matching a query string. The\n//  results can be piped into downstream actions (e.g. Open Contact).\n//\n\nimport AppIntents\nimport Foundation\n\nstruct FindContactIntent: AppIntent {\n    static let title: LocalizedStringResource = \"Find Contact\"\n    static let description = IntentDescription(\n        \"Search ContactManager by name, company, email, or notes.\"\n    )\n\n    @Parameter(title: \"Query\") var query: String\n\n    @MainActor\n    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult & ReturnsValue<[ContactEntity]> {\n        let matches = try await ContactEntityQuery().entities(matching: query)\n        return .result(value: matches)\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/SpotlightIndexer.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  SpotlightIndexer.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Pushes contacts into Spotlight's index. The first launch indexes the\n//  full set; subsequent calls do the same — the contact corpus stays\n//  modest enough that a full reindex on every mutation is cheaper than\n//  tracking per-row deltas.\n//\n\nimport CoreSpotlight\nimport Foundation\n\nenum SpotlightIndexer {\n    /// Identifier scope so we can clear *our* items without touching\n    /// anything else Spotlight has indexed for this app.\n    static let domainIdentifier = \"com.scottdensmore.ContactManager.contacts\"\n\n    /// Replaces our entire indexed set with the supplied entities. Errors\n    /// are logged but not surfaced — Spotlight indexing failure is a\n    /// quality-of-life regression, not a user-visible error worth alerting.\n    static func reindex(_ entities: [ContactEntity]) async {\n        let index = CSSearchableIndex.default()\n        let items = entities.map { entity in\n            CSSearchableItem(\n                uniqueIdentifier: entity.id,\n                domainIdentifier: domainIdentifier,\n                attributeSet: entity.attributeSet\n            )\n        }\n        do {\n            try await index.deleteSearchableItems(withDomainIdentifiers: [domainIdentifier])\n            if !items.isEmpty {\n                try await index.indexSearchableItems(items)\n            }\n        } catch {\n            print(\"Spotlight reindex failed: \\(error)\")\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

Fired\n            // after the save commits so observers see the post-mutation state.\n            NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .contactsDidChange, object: nil)\n            return result\n        } catch {\n            context.rollback()\n            undoManager?.endUndoGrouping()\n            throw error\n        }\n    }\n}"

  "content": "//\n//  ContentView+Import.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Import handlers (system Contacts, vCard file picker, vCard URL drops)\n//  factored out of `ContentView` so the main view stays focused on\n//  composition and state. Each handler runs the parse off the main\n//  actor and routes inserts through `ContactStore` so they participate\n//  in the existing Undo group.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport SwiftUI\n\nextension ContentView {\n    // MARK: - System Contacts import\n\n    func importSystemContacts() {\n        Task {\n            // Permission prompt + fetch + mapping all run off the main actor;\n            // only the final insert hops back here.\n            let parsed: [ParsedContact]\n            do {\n                parsed = try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {\n                    try await ContactsBridge.fetchAllParsed()\n                }.value\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                return\n            }\n            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {\n                errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in your system Contacts.\"\n                return\n            }\n            do {\n                try store.importContacts(parsed)\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - vCard import\n\n    /// Imports one or more vCard files dropped onto the contact list.\n    func importVCardURLs(_ urls: [URL]) {\n        Task {\n            let parsed: [ParsedContact] = await Task.detached {\n                var all: [ParsedContact] = []\n                for url in urls {\n                    let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()\n                    defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }\n                    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),\n                          let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)\n                    else { continue }\n                    all.append(contentsOf: VCard.parse(text))\n                }\n                return all\n            }.value\n\n            guard !parsed.isEmpty else {\n                errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in that file.\"\n                return\n            }\n            do {\n                try store.importContacts(parsed)\n            } catch {\n                errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    func handleImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {\n        switch result {\n        case .failure(let error):\n            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n        case .success(let url):\n            Task {\n                // Read and parse off the main actor so large files don't block UI.\n                let parsed: [ParsedContact]? = await Task.detached {\n                    let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()\n                    defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }\n                    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),\n                          let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }\n                    return VCard.parse(text)\n                }.value\n\n                guard let parsed else {\n                    errorMessage = \"That file couldn't be read as a vCard.\"\n                    return\n                }\n                guard !parsed.isEmpty else {\n                    errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in that file.\"\n                    return\n                }\n                do {\n                    try store.importContacts(parsed)\n                } catch {\n                    errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n"

ContactManager/Views/ContentView.swift:150
  `contactsDidChange` assumes `@Query contacts` has already refreshed. For deletes/inserts, `contacts` can still reflect the pre-save fetch when the notification arrives, causing Spotlight to reindex stale data (e.g., deleted contacts remain indexed). ContactManager/Support/SpotlightIndexer.swift:39
  `reindex(_:)` can be called multiple times in quick succession (initial indexing + per-mutation indexing). Because it does a delete-then-index, concurrent calls can interleave and leave Spotlight with an older snapshot (or even an empty index if a later delete wins). Serialize reindex operations within `SpotlightIndexer`.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contactmanager/ContactManager/Support/SpotlightIndexer.swift",
  "content": "//\n//  SpotlightIndexer.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  Pushes contacts into Spotlight's index. An actor so back-to-back calls\n//  during a burst of mutations serialize cleanly — a delete-then-index\n//  pair must not interleave with another pair or Spotlight ends up\n//  reflecting an older snapshot (or empty).\n//\n//  Each call fetches a fresh snapshot via `ContactEntityQuery` instead of\n//  trusting a caller-supplied list, because `@Query`'s post-save refresh\n//  is asynchronous and can lag a `ContactStore.mutate` notification.\n//\n\nimport CoreSpotlight\nimport Foundation\n\nactor SpotlightIndexer {\n    static let shared = SpotlightIndexer()\n\n    /// Identifier scope so we can clear *our* items without touching\n    /// anything else Spotlight has indexed for this app.\n    static let domainIdentifier = \"com.scottdensmore.ContactManager.contacts\"\n\n    /// Replaces our entire indexed set with a freshly-fetched snapshot.\n    /// Errors are logged but not surfaced — a Spotlight indexing failure\n    /// is a quality-of-life regression, not a user-visible error.\n    func reindex() async {\n        let entities = (try? await ContactEntityQuery().allEntities()) ?? []\n        let index = CSSearchableIndex.default()\n        let items = entities.map { entity in\n            CSSearchableItem(\n                uniqueIdentifier: entity.id,\n                domainIdentifier: Self.domainIdentifier,\n                attributeSet: entity.attributeSet\n            )\n        }\n        do {\n            try await index.deleteSearchableItems(withDomainIdentifiers: [Self.domainIdentifier])\n            if !items.isEmpty {\n                try await index.indexSearchableItems(items)\n            }\n        } catch {\n            print(\"Spotlight reindex failed: \\(error)\")\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//\n//  EntityModelContainer.swift\n//  ContactManager\n//\n//  A process-wide handle to the app's `ModelContainer`. App Intents and\n//  CoreSpotlight queries need to read contacts without going through the\n//  SwiftUI environment; the app sets this once after `loadContainer()`\n//  succeeds and the entity query reads it from any actor.\n//\n//  Access is guarded by an `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` so concurrent reads\n//  during a launch-time setup are well-defined. The lock is held only\n//  long enough to read or write the container reference itself.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\nimport os\nimport SwiftData\n\nenum EntityModelContainer {\n    private static let storage = OSAllocatedUnfairLock<ModelContainer?>(initialState: nil)\n\n    /// The shared container, populated by `ContactManagerApp` after the\n    /// store loads. `nil` if loading failed or we're running under tests.\n    static var shared: ModelContainer? {\n        get { storage.withLock { $0 } }\n        set { storage.withLock { $0 = newValue } }\n    }\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

All five comments addressed in `33337e2`:

| Concern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Stale `@Query` snapshot at reindex time | Indexer fetches its own snapshot via `ContactEntityQuery` — `@Query` refresh is async and can still reflect pre-save state when `contactsDidChange` fires. |
| Concurrent `reindex()` interleave | `SpotlightIndexer` is now an `actor`; delete + index pairs serialize. |
| `nonisolated(unsafe) static var` race | Guarded with `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` (held only across get/set). |
| Whitespace-only subtitle text | `subtitleText` uses a private `String.isBlank` helper that matches `Contact.primaryEmail`/`subtitle` semantics. |
| Whitespace-only field values indexed | Snapshot init filters fields with the same `isBlank` check. |

CI green; ready to merge whenever.

> AGENT

My pick is **K — CSV import**. It's the smallest user-facing feature left and the most common migration path (Google Contacts exports CSV by default, Outlook/Excel do too). Pure code, no entitlements, builds on the existing `ParsedContact` + `ContactStore.importContacts` pipeline you already have for vCard and macOS Contacts.

Tradeoff: CSV is famously messy — quoted fields with embedded commas/newlines, different exporters use different column headers, mismatched row lengths. The first PR can scope to header-based auto-detection for the two big formats (Google Contacts + Apple/Outlook), and surface a clear error if the headers can't be matched. A column-mapping UI is a follow-up if needed.

Want me to start it, or pick something else? (I multi-window and D Swift 6 strict concurrency are the other genuinely useful ones; D has no user-facing change.)

Address 2+ is intentionally dropped; we don't have\n//    multi-address support today.\n//  - Custom-labelled email/phone columns (\"Home Phone\", \"E-mail 1 -\n//    Value\", etc.) collect into the contact's `emails`/`phones` list\n//    in column order, preserving the label encoded in the header.\n//\n\nimport Foundation\n\nenum CSV {\n    // MARK: - Parsing\n\n    /// Parses a CSV document into rows of fields. UTF-8 BOM (`\\u{FEFF}`) is stripped.\n    static func parse(_ text: String) -> [[String]] {\n        var input = text\n        if input.first == \"\\u{FEFF}\" { input.removeFirst() }\n\n        var rows: [[String]] = []\n        var row: [String] = []\n        var field = \"\"\n        var inQuotes = false\n        var i = input.startIndex\n\n        while i < input.endIndex {\n            let c = input[i]\n            if inQuotes {\n                if c == \"\\\"\" {\n                    let next = input.index(after: i)\n                    if next < input.endIndex, input[next] == \"\\\"\" {\n                        // Escaped quote.\n                        field.append(\"\\\"\")\n                        i = input.index(after: next)\n                        continue\n                    }\n                    inQuotes = false\n                } else {\n                    field.append(c)\n                }\n            } else {\n                switch c {\n                case \"\\\"\":\n                    inQuotes = true\n                case \",\":\n                    row.append(field)\n                    field = \"\"\n                case \"\\r\":\n                    row.append(field)\n                    rows.append(row)\n                    field = \"\"\n                    row = []\n                    let next = input.index(after: i)\n                    if next < input.endIndex, input[next] == \"\\n\" {\n                        i = next\n                    }\n                case \"\\n\":\n                    row.append(field)\n                    rows.append(row)\n                    field = \"\"\n                    row = []\n                default:\n                    field.append(c)\n                }\n            }\n            i = input.index(after: i)\n        }\n        // Trailing field/row when the file doesn't end with a newline.\n        if !field.isEmpty || !row.isEmpty {\n            row.append(field)\n            rows.append(row)\n        }\n        return rows\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Mapping\n\n    /// Parses a CSV contact export. parseContacts(_ text: String) -> [ParsedContact]? {\n        var rows = parse(text)\n        guard let headers = rows.first else { return nil }\n        rows.removeFirst()\n\n        let columns = headers.map(column(forHeader:))\n        guard columns.contains(where: { $0 != nil }) else { return nil }\n\n        return rows.compactMap { row in\n            let contact = makeContact(row: row, columns: columns)\n            // Skip rows where literally nothing mapped — empty trailing\n            // lines or schema-only stub rows shouldn't become contacts.\n            return contact.isEmpty ? nil : contact\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static func makeContact(\n        row: [String], columns: [Column?]\n    ) -> ParsedContact {\n        var parsed = ParsedContact()\n .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n            guard !value.isEmpty else { continue }\n            apply(column: column, value: value, to: &parsed)\n        }\n        // If only a full-name column was set (no case .scalar(.firstName): parsed.firstName = value\n        case .scalar(.lastName): parsed.lastName = value\n        case .scalar(.fullName): parsed.fullNameSeed = value\n        case    case .scalar(.postalCode): parsed.postalCode = value\n        case .scalar(.country): parsed.country = value\n        case .email(let label): parsed.emails.append((label, value))\n        case .phone(let label): parsed.phones.append((label, value))\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static func splitName(_ name: String, into parsed: inout ParsedContact) {\n        let trimmed = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)\n        if let lastSpace = trimmed.lastIndex(of: \" \") {\n            parsed.firstName = String(trimmed[..<lastSpace])\n                .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n            parsed.lastName = String(trimmed[trimmed.index(after: lastSpace)...])\n                .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)\n        } else {\n            parsed.firstName = trimmed\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static let isoBirthdayFormatter: DateFormatter = {\n        let df = DateFormatter()\n        df.locale = Locale(identifier: \"en_US_POSIX\")\n        df.dateFormat = \"yyyy-MM-dd\"\n        df.timeZone = .autoupdatingCurrent\n        return df\n    }()\n\n    private static func parseBirthday(_ value: String) -> Date? {\n        isoBirthdayFormatter.date(from: value)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Header → column\n\n    /// Internal column kinds. Scalars overwrite the matching `ParsedContact`\n    /// field; `.email`/`.phone` append to their list so multiple\n    /// columns map to multiple values.\n    enum Column: Equatable {\n        case scalar(Scalar)\n        case email(FieldLabel)\n        case phone(FieldLabel)\n\n        enum Scalar: Equatable {\n            case firstName, lastName, fullName\n            case company, jobTitle, notes, birthday\n            case street, city, state, postalCode, country\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Matches a single CSV header cell. Returns `nil` for headers we\n    /// don't model (custom fields, separator columns like \"E-mail 1 -\n    /// Type\"). The lookup is case- and punctuation-insensitive.\n    static func column(forHeader raw: String) -> Column? {\n        let h = normalize(raw)\n        switch h {\n        case \"firstname\", \"givenname\":\n            return .scalar(.firstName)\n        case \"lastname\", \"surname\", \"familyname\":\n            return .scalar(.lastName)\n        case \"name\", \"fullname\", \"displayname\":\n            return .scalar(.fullName)\n        case \"company\", \"companyname\", \"organization\", \"organizationname\":\n            return .scalar(.company)\n        case \"jobtitle\", \"title\", \"organizationtitle\", \"position\":\n            return .scalar(.jobTitle)\n        case \"notes\", \"note\":\n            return .scalar(.notes)\n        case \"birthday\", \"dob\", \"dateofbirth\":\n            return .scalar(.birthday)\n        case \"street\", \"address\", \"streetaddress\",\n             \"homestreet\", \"businessstreet\":\n            return .scalar(.street)\n        case \"city\", \"homecity\", \"businesscity\":\n            return .scalar(.city)\n        case \"state\", \"region\", \"province\",\n             \"homestate\", \"businessstate\":\n            return .scalar(.state)\n        case \"zip\", \"zipcode\", \"postalcode\",\n             \"homepostalcode\", \"businesspostalcode\":\n            return .scalar(.postalCode)\n        case \"country\", \"homecountry\", \"businesscountry\":\n            return .scalar(.country)\n        case \"email\", \"emailaddress\", \"primaryemail\",\n             \"homeemail\", \"personalemail\":\n            return .email(.home)\n        case \"workemail\", \"businessemail\":\n            return .email(.work)\n        case \"phone\", \"phonenumber\", \"primaryphone\":\n            return .phone(.mobile)\n        case \"homephone\":\n            return .phone(.home)\n        case \"workphone\", \"businessphone\":\n            return .phone(.work)\n        case \"mobilephone\", \"mobile\", \"cellphone\", \"cell\":\n            return .phone(.mobile)\n        case \"mainphone\":\n            return .phone(.main)\n        case \"otherphone\":\n            return .phone(.other)\n        default:\n            break\n        }\n        // Google Contacts \"Address 1 - …\" columns.\n        if let suffix = stripPrefix(h, prefix: \"address1\") {\n            switch suffix {\n            case \"street\": return .scalar(.street)\n            case \"city\": return .scalar(.city)\n            case \"region\", \"state\": return .scalar(.state)\n            case \"postalcode\": return .scalar(.postalCode)\n            case \"country\": return .scalar(.country)\n            default: return nil\n            }\n        }\n        // Google's indexed multi-value columns: \"E-mail 1 - Value\" /\n        // \"Phone 2 - Value\". After normalize: \"email1value\" / \"phone2value\".\n        if isIndexedColumn(h, base: \"email\", suffix: \"value\") {\n            return .email(.home)\n        }\n        if isIndexedColumn(h, base: \"phone\", suffix: \"value\") {\n            return .phone(.mobile)\n        }\n        return nil\n    }\n\n    /// Lowercases and strips characters that vary across exporters (spaces,\n    /// hyphens, underscores, slashes, dots) so headers compare structurally.\n    private static func normalize(_ raw: String) -> String {\n        var out = \"\"\n        out.reserveCapacity(raw.count)\n        for c in raw.lowercased() where c.isLetter || c.isNumber {\n            out.append(c)\n        }\n        return out\n    }\n\n    private static func stripPrefix(_ haystack: String, prefix: String) -> String? {\n        guard haystack.hasPrefix(prefix) else { return nil }\n        return String(haystack.dropFirst(prefix.count))\n    }\n\n    private static func isIndexedColumn(_ h: String, base: String, suffix: String) -> Bool {\n        guard h.hasPrefix(base), h.hasSuffix(suffix) else { return false }\n        let middle = h.dropFirst(base.count).dropLast(suffix.count)\n        return !middle.isEmpty && middle.allSatisfy(\\.isNumber)\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - ParsedContact helpers used during CSV mapping\n\nextension ParsedContact {\n    /// Considered \"empty\" for the purpose of dropping schema-only stub\n    /// rows: every scalar field is blank and there are no fields/photos.\n    var isEmpty: Bool {\n        firstName.isEmpty && lastName.isEmpty && company.isEmpty\n            && jobTitle.isEmpty && notes.isEmpty && birthday == nil\n            && street.isEmpty && city.isEmpty && state.isEmpty\n            && postalCode.isEmpty && country.isEmpty\n            && emails.isEmpty && phones.isEmpty\n            && photoData == nil && fullNameSeed.isEmpty\n    }\n}\n"

  "old_string": "    func handleImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {",
  "new_string": "    // MARK: - CSV import\n\n    func handleCSVImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {\n        switch result {\n        case .failure(let error):\n            errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n        case .success(let url):\n            Task {\n                let outcome: CSVImportOutcome = await Task.detached {\n                    let didAccess = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()\n                    defer { if didAccess { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }\n                    guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else { return .unreadable }\n                    // CSV exports are commonly UTF-8 but Excel still emits\n                    // UTF-16 with a BOM; try both before giving up.\n                    let text: String\n                    if let utf8 = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) {\n                        text = utf8\n                    } else if let utf16 = String(data: data, encoding: .utf16) {\n                        text = utf16\n                    } else {\n                        return .unreadable\n                    }\n                    guard let parsed = CSV.parseContacts(text) else { return .unrecognized }\n                    return .parsed(parsed)\n                }.value\n\n                switch outcome {\n                case .unreadable:\n                    errorMessage = \"That file couldn't be read as a CSV.\"\n                case .unrecognized:\n                    errorMessage = \"Couldn't recognize the CSV — the header row \" +\n                        \"doesn't include any known contact columns (e.g. First Name, \" +\n                        \"Email, Phone).\"\n                case .parsed(let contacts) where contacts.isEmpty:\n                    errorMessage = \"No contacts were found in that file.\"\n                case .parsed(let contacts):\n                    do {\n                        try store.importContacts(contacts)\n                    } catch {\n                        errorMessage = error.localizedDescription\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    func handleImport(_ result: Result<URL, Error>) {"
}

  "new_string": "    static func parse(_ text: String) -> [[String]] {\n        var input = text\n        if input.first == \"\\u{FEFF}\" { input.removeFirst() }\n\n        var state = ParseState()\n        var cursor = input.startIndex\n        while cursor < input.endIndex {\n            let char = input[cursor]\n            cursor = state.inQuotes\n                ? state.handleQuoted(char: char, cursor: cursor, in: input)\n                : state.handleUnquoted(char: char, cursor: cursor, in: input)\n        }\n        // Trailing field/row when the file doesn't end with a newline.\n        if !state.field.isEmpty || !state.row.isEmpty {\n            state.endRow()\n        }\n        return state.rows\n    }\n\n    /// Mutable scratchpad used by `parse(_:)`. Pulled out so each\n    /// transition stays small enough for SwiftLint's body-length budget.\n    private struct ParseState {\n        var rows: [[String]] = []\n        var row: [String] = []\n        var field = \"\"\n        var inQuotes = false\n\n        mutating func endField() { row.append(field); field = \"\" }\n        mutating func endRow() { endField(); rows.append(row); row = [] }\n\n        mutating func handleQuoted(char: Character, cursor: String.Index, in input: String) -> String.Index {\n            if char == \"\\\"\" {\n                let next = input.index(after: cursor)\n                if next < input.endIndex, input[next] == \"\\\"\" {\n                    // Doubled-quote escape: keep one literal quote.\n                    field.append(\"\\\"\")\n                    return input.index(after: next)\n                }\n                inQuotes = false\n            } else {\n                field.append(char)\n            }\n            return input.index(after: cursor)\n        }\n\n        mutating func handleUnquoted(\n            char: Character, cursor: String.Index, in input: String\n        ) -> String.Index {\n            switch char {\n            case \"\\\"\": inQuotes = true\n            case \",\": endField()\n            case \"\\n\": endRow()\n            case \"\\r\":\n                endRow()\n                let next = input.index(after: cursor)\n                // Consume the LF half of CRLF so it doesn't open a blank row.\n                if next < input.endIndex, input[next] == \"\\n\" {\n                    return input.index(after: next)\n                }\n            default: field.append(char)\n            }\n            return input.index(after: cursor)\n        }\n    }"
}

  "new_string": "        mutating func handleUnquoted(\n            char: Character, cursor: String.Index, in input: String\n        ) -> String.Index {\n            switch char {\n            case \"\\\"\": inQuotes = true\n            case \",\": endField()\n            // Swift collapses CRLF into a single `Character`, so the third\n            // case below catches `\\r\\n` files (Windows / Excel exports);\n            // standalone `\\r` (classic Mac) still wraps the row.\n            case \"\\n\", \"\\r\", \"\\r\\n\": endRow()\n            default: field.append(char)\n            }\n            return input.index(after: cursor)\n        }"
}

> AGENT

PR #36 is up: https://github.com/scottdensmore/contactmanager/pull/36

What landed:
- **`CSV.swift`** — RFC-4180-ish reader (CRLF/LF, quoted commas/newlines, `""` escapes, BOM stripping) plus header-based mapper for Google Contacts and Outlook/Apple forms.
- **`ContentView+Import.swift`** — `handleCSVImport` with UTF-8 → UTF-16 fallback for Excel exports and distinct alerts for unreadable vs unrecognized CSVs.
- **App menu** — `File ▸ Import CSV…` added below the existing import items.
- 21 new `CSVTests` cover the parser corner cases and the mapper.

Notable spec detail discovered along the way: Swift treats `\r\n` as a single `Character` (extended grapheme cluster), so the switch handles it as its own case rather than using lookahead.

CI running; I'll address any Copilot feedback when it lands. Worth eyeballing on your end after CI: export your Google Contacts as CSV, import it, confirm names/emails/phones/labels look right; then try **Edit ▸ Undo Import Contacts** to roll back.

> AGENT

My pick is **I — Multi-window**. The last genuinely user-facing feature on the list: open a contact in its own window via right-click "Open in New Window" or ⌘⌥-click. Each detached window has its own toolbar, its own undo stack, and survives the main window closing. Real Mac power-user behavior — think Finder windows or Mail's "Open Message in New Window".

Tradeoff: SwiftUI's `WindowGroup(for: Value.self)` needs the value to be `Hashable & Codable`. We already encode `PersistentIdentifier` via the helper from PR #32, so the plumbing is straightforward — but each new window needs its own `modelContainer` injection and its own `EntityModelContainer.shared` is already in place, so reusing that works. Scope-wise the first PR is "open in new window" via menu/context-menu, leaving multi-window settings (zoom/position persistence) as a follow-up if you want it.

Want me to start it, or pick something else? (C UI tests via XCUITest and D Swift 6 strict concurrency are the other items left; both are infrastructure, not user-facing.)

Worth eyeballing on your end after CI:
- Right-click a row → "Open in New Window" opens a detached window with that contact's detail.
- Edit in the detached window → change reflects in the main window (shared `ContactStore`).
- Delete the contact from the main window → detached window flips to "Contact Not Found".
- ⌘W closes only the detached window; main keeps running.
